note: Plain-language descriptions of the recorded questions and results. Original claims, statuses, sources and dependencies remain unchanged. Reading order is navigation, not a newly asserted research lineage.

P2R0.title: Mean outputs from network weights
P2R0.summary: Estimate each neuron’s average output directly from the weights, without running sampled inputs through the network.

P2R0A.title: Scoring and computation limits
P2R0A.summary: Establish how prediction error is scored and how much computation, memory and time an estimator may use.
P2R0A.result: The Phase 2 limits were 2⁴¹ metered FLOPs, 120 seconds and 8 GB of memory, with a separate 0.4-second control-time limit.

P2R0B.title: Adapting to wider, deeper networks
P2R0B.summary: Reuse the mathematical formulas from smaller networks, then remeasure the choices that depend on network size.
P2R0B.result: The identities transferred. Fitted coefficients, retained tensor sizes and layer schedules needed new measurements.

P2R0C.title: Accuracy versus computation cost
P2R0C.summary: Measure how reducing arithmetic changes the official score, which depends on both prediction error and computation.
P2R0C.result: A cheaper implementation improved the official score. Reducing prediction error remained the next target.

P2R0C1.title: Balancing accuracy and computation
P2R0C1.summary: Compare complete estimators by the error and computation cost measured separately on each network.
P2R0C1.result: The replacement passed local and client/server checks but failed in official submission; the failure could not be reproduced. The previous scored estimator remained the reference.

P2R0C1D.title: Comparing estimator implementations
P2R0C1D.summary: Try alternative ways to store and propagate statistical information, then check their accuracy and actual running cost.
P2R0C1D.result: The attempted replacement passed local and client/server tests, but its submission failures remained unexplained.

P2R0D.title: Gaussian and Hermite approximations
P2R0D.summary: Approximate each layer’s distribution with a Gaussian, then add Hermite polynomial terms to capture departures from it.
P2R0D.result: Order 4 reached final-layer mean-squared error 3.85 × 10⁻⁶. Higher orders gave essentially no improvement.

P2R0E.title: Tracking more than mean and variance
P2R0E.summary: Carry higher-order statistics through the network to capture distribution shape that a Gaussian approximation misses.
P2R0E.result: The surviving Q24 implementation reached mean-squared error 5.77 × 10⁻⁷, above the 10⁻⁸ target. The tested higher-order variants were closed.

P2R0E1.title: Fitting richer models into the budget
P2R0E1.summary: Revisit distribution approximations rejected under earlier, tighter computation-cost targets.
P2R0E1.result: A fourth-order state retaining 2,048 terms fit inside the Phase 2 computation limit.

P2R0E2.title: Finding why error starts at layer 3
P2R0E2.summary: Separate errors in the supplied layer statistics from errors in the formulas that use those statistics.
P2R0E2.result: The run stopped on a sandbox restriction before producing a scientific result.

P2R0E3.title: Propagating third and fourth cumulants
P2R0E3.summary: Carry third- and fourth-order information from one layer to the next, including relationships between different neurons.
P2R0E3.result: The equations and implementation were verified within computation and memory limits. Accuracy still required separate tests.

P2R0E3A.title: Testing each higher-order term
P2R0E3A.summary: Remove correction terms one at a time to measure which ones improve the final prediction.
P2R0E3A.result: The planned accuracy comparison could not start: stored statistics failed consistency checks, and simplified variants failed preliminary tests.

P2R0F.title: Learning corrections from training data
P2R0F.summary: Fit a model to the errors in the propagated statistics, then use its corrections as the estimator moves through the network.
P2R0F.result: With accurate reference inputs, the correction beat 10⁻⁸ mean-squared error. With the estimator’s own inputs, the best verified result was about 3.23 × 10⁻⁸.

P2R0F1.title: Corrections with reference inputs
P2R0F1.summary: Supply accurate intermediate values to measure how much error the learned correction could remove.
P2R0F1.result: Error fell below 10⁻⁸, but the supplied reference values were not available during deployed inference.

P2R0F2.title: Corrections with estimated inputs
P2R0F2.summary: Feed the correction model only quantities the estimator can compute itself, then check whether the gains survive through the network.
P2R0F2.result: The tested implementations either failed to improve accuracy or exceeded the control-time limit.

P2R0F3.title: Designing propagation and correction together
P2R0F3.summary: Check whether improving the underlying estimator also improves the output of its learned correction.
P2R0F3.result: In the tested models, improving the base estimator did not improve the corrected output. The study selected a more accurate base estimator as the next design direction.

P2R0G.title: Recovering information in later layers
P2R0G.summary: Find which statistical information the later layers need, then work out how to compute it from the network weights.
P2R0G.result: The tested signed-pair correction failed, and the broader source search found no viable candidate. Computing better later-layer corrections directly from the weights remained open.

P2R0G11.title: Why local gains failed in evaluation
P2R0G11.summary: Compare local and official test results for a learned correction, then investigate why its apparent improvement disappeared.
P2R0G11.result: The correction looked better locally but scored worse in official evaluation. Refitting did not beat the existing estimator.

P2R0G18.title: Pair-based corrections in later layers
P2R0G18.summary: Test a family of pair-based corrections for the predictions in the later layers.
P2R0G18.result: The three-bank correction failed its accuracy test, and the broader source search found zero viable cases among 315. The remaining proposal lacked a required source; every recorded subroute had ended or was blocked.

P2R0G18B.title: Testing a three-bank pair correction
P2R0G18B.summary: Check whether the fixed signed-pair model improves the final prediction over the existing estimator.
P2R0G18B.result: Mean-squared error was 3.02 × 10⁻⁸, about 2.84% worse than the comparison submission. This tested formulation was rejected.

P2R0G19.title: Later-layer corrections from weights
P2R0G19.summary: Replace supplied reference corrections with quantities calculated directly from the network weights.
P2R0G19.result: Supplying reference corrections in layers 10–15 reduced error below 10⁻⁸. Computing those corrections within the budget remained open.

P2R0G19B.title: Passing corrections from layer to layer
P2R0G19B.summary: Compute each layer’s correction from earlier layers, retaining enough information to improve the final prediction.
P2R0G19B.result: Reference inputs showed enough correction capacity to reach the accuracy target, but three learned ways of supplying those inputs failed. A small diagnostic study remained active.

P2R0G19B_CARRIER.title: Computing cross-neuron third moments
P2R0G19B_CARRIER.summary: Compute third-order relationships between pairs of neurons accurately enough to improve the final prediction, within the computation budget.
P2R0G19B_CARRIER.result: The affordable approximations still fell short of the required fidelity. Several compression and transport alternatives added no useful signal, leaving an accurate, affordable supplier unresolved.

P2R0G19B_MATH_ACCELERATION.title: Making higher-order corrections affordable
P2R0G19B_MATH_ACCELERATION.summary: Find formulas that preserve the useful third- and fourth-order corrections while reducing the arithmetic and storage they require.
P2R0G19B_MATH_ACCELERATION.result: An affordable complete correction with a bound on the remaining error had not yet been derived. This record describes mathematical proposals, not a passing estimator.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_H2H3_ENDPOINT_ADJOINT.title: Tracing final error backward through layers
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_H2H3_ENDPOINT_ADJOINT.summary: Work backward from the final prediction to identify which variance and third-moment information must be computed.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_H2H3_ENDPOINT_ADJOINT.result: The backward calculation identifies needed projections without carrying the full third-moment tensor. The complete method still needed to pass its cost and end-to-end accuracy tests.

P2R0G19B_MECH_ROOT.title: Where final-layer error comes from
P2R0G19B_MECH_ROOT.summary: Trace the output error to mistakes in the variance and higher-order statistics carried through each layer.
P2R0G19B_MECH_ROOT.result: Replacing those statistics with accurate reference values reduced error to the reference noise level on both tested networks.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1_OPEN_PROBLEM.title: Correcting errors the learned model misses
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1_OPEN_PROBLEM.summary: Compute later-layer variance and third-moment corrections that add information the deployed learned model does not already capture.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1_OPEN_PROBLEM.result: Accurate reference variance and third-moment corrections helped, but tested substitutes did not transfer reliably. Computing useful corrections cheaply remained unresolved.

P2R0H.title: Testing an estimator before submission
P2R0H.summary: Check a complete estimator’s accuracy, running time and memory use before submitting it to the official evaluation.
P2R0H.result: Submission #328586 ran successfully but remained above the desired accuracy. A better candidate had to pass the required checks before another submission.

P2R0H3.title: Repairing rare large prediction errors
P2R0H3.summary: Find networks with unusually large prediction errors and verify the repair across the full test population.
P2R0H3.result: All 11 failing cases among 688 tested networks were brought below the registered error threshold of 5 × 10⁻⁷.

P2R0E4.title: Running the higher-order estimator within limits
P2R0E4.summary: Implement the richer statistical model and measure its computation, memory, elapsed time and control-time overhead.
P2R0E4.result: Q24 ran all 100 evaluation networks within the resource limits, closing the implementation task. Its mean-squared error of 5.77 × 10⁻⁷ still missed the 10⁻⁸ accuracy target.

P2R0F3A1.title: Preserving a discarded fourth-order correction
P2R0F3A1.summary: Carry the mixed fourth-moment correction K22 between layers instead of discarding it at each reset.
P2R0F3A1.result: The base estimator’s error fell by 35.6% in a 200-network pilot. The learned correction already captured nearly all of that gain.

P2R0G2A.title: Exact formulas for directional corrections
P2R0G2A.summary: Combine the second- through fifth-order correction formulas and verify them against direct calculations.
P2R0G2A.result: Exact small-network checks passed. This established the formulas, not a complete deployable estimator.

P2R0G18B4.title: Final accuracy test of the signed-pair model
P2R0G18B4.summary: Evaluate the frozen signed-pair model against the prediction-error threshold fixed before the test.
P2R0G18B4.result: The model missed the accuracy threshold: mean-squared error was 3.02 × 10⁻⁸. The test was final for this version.

P2R0G19B_K31_FRAME_SECANT_ACTION.title: Updating the mixed fourth-moment correction
P2R0G19B_K31_FRAME_SECANT_ACTION.summary: Combine changes in the K31 source, the formula consuming it and the coordinate frame without counting the same correction twice.
P2R0G19B_K31_FRAME_SECANT_ACTION.result: An exact update combining changes in the source, the readout and the coordinate frame still needed to be derived, with a bound on its error and stability.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_CORE_ONLY_FIDELITY_NOGO.title: A quadratic core misses fourth-order information
P2R0G19B_NCQC_CORE_ONLY_FIDELITY_NOGO.summary: Check whether the quadratic part of the distribution model is sufficient without its remaining fourth-order correction.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_CORE_ONLY_FIDELITY_NOGO.result: The quadratic core missed most of the remaining fourth-order contribution. The additional correction could not be dropped.

P2R0G19B_AQ_D10_SEMANTICS_FORK.title: Replacing a distribution versus correcting it
P2R0G19B_AQ_D10_SEMANTICS_FORK.summary: Separate two mathematical choices: replace the Gaussian model, or keep it and add corrections.
P2R0G19B_AQ_D10_SEMANTICS_FORK.result: The two choices use different covariance formulas. Their accuracy and cost claims cannot be combined.

P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_IDENTITY.title: A cheaper fourth-order contraction formula
P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_IDENTITY.summary: Use a sum of fourth powers to evaluate the Price contraction through matrix products.
P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_IDENTITY.result: An exact identity replaces a generic Hessian operation with structured matrix products.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_CANONICAL_DIRECT_APPLY_CAP.title: Dense inverse application exceeds the budget
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CANONICAL_DIRECT_APPLY_CAP.summary: Count the minimum work required to apply the proposed dense right inverse.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CANONICAL_DIRECT_APPLY_CAP.result: Even the optimistic cost exceeded the limit before adding the remaining corrections.

P2R0G19B_QHEAD_PRODUCT86.title: Adding four features to the learned correction
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_PRODUCT86.summary: Test whether four additional input features improve the existing 82-feature correction model.
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_PRODUCT86.result: The model recovered only about 0.094% of the available improvement, below the required 8%.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_I_EMISSION.title: Fixing the fourth-moment update through ReLU
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_I_EMISSION.summary: Correct the K31 update, whose formula omitted non-Gaussian terms when passing through the activation function.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_I_EMISSION.result: After the fix, the one-step K31 calculation correlated about 0.998 with the reference, up from 0.33.

P2R0E4A.title: Faster correlation powers for Q24
P2R0E4A.summary: Compute the same Q24 correlation powers with a simpler recurrence to reduce runtime without changing estimator output.
P2R0E4A.result: Matched the parent bit for bit and passed the full-size resource test. Wall time fell 14%; accuracy was not retested because the output was unchanged.

P2R0E3A5.title: Can the stored moments describe a real distribution?
P2R0E3A5.summary: Check whether the stored higher moments satisfy necessary determinant inequalities, allowing explicitly for rounding error.
P2R0E3A5.result: Certified 22 negative determinants in layers 10–16. None could be explained by rounding, so these moment tuples were invalid.

P2R0H3A.title: Repair invalid moments with a two-point distribution
P2R0H3A.summary: Replace invalid marginal moments by a two-point distribution that preserves the first two moments.
P2R0H3A.result: The repair left invalid determinants, made four previously finite cases nonfinite, and rescued no failures. This particular repair was rejected; joint or scale-aware repairs remain open.

P2R0H3G.title: Retired H1 observability repair design
P2R0H3G.summary: Consider an H1 observability change as a possible explanation for the stability failure.
P2R0H3G.result: The variance-floor equality defect supplied a different diagnosis. This design was retired before implementation or testing; it provides no accuracy result.

P2R0H7.title: Deploy the learned correction inside Q24
P2R0H7.summary: Train the correction on features produced by Q24 itself, then verify that the combined estimator can run within the challenge limits.
P2R0H7.result: Submission #328326 passed grading with raw MSE 2.940964e−8. The successful estimator used one host; the separate two-host version remained over budget.

P2R0F2D.title: Predict accumulated error with four learned states
P2R0F2D.summary: Use four learned states to correct errors as the estimator runs through the network, and test all 688 networks by fourfold cross-validation.
P2R0F2D.result: Out-of-fold MSE fell to 3.296948e−8, 63.83% below the uncorrected host, but missed the required improvement and 1e−8 target. No runtime test followed.

P2R0F2J.title: Use channel energy to predict correction errors
P2R0F2J.summary: Add per-channel transport energy and coherence features to the learned correction, then test across all 688 networks.
P2R0F2J.result: Out-of-fold MSE reached 3.233496e−8 but missed both mean and worst-network targets. A separate feature pass also put this version above the compute budget.

P2R0F2O.title: Blend five correction models
P2R0F2O.summary: Test whether averaging or cross-validated nonnegative blends of five correction models can remove their remaining errors.
P2R0F2O.result: The best valid blend reached 3.221703e−8 and missed the improvement threshold. Even optimistic fits barely helped: the models made too many of the same errors.

P2R0C1D3.title: Correct a cheaper rank-16,384 mean propagator
P2R0C1D3.summary: Pair a cheaper recursive mean estimator with a correction trained on that estimator’s own features.
P2R0C1D3.result: The protected test gave raw MSE 7.429440e−7, about 21 times its cost-adjusted break-even target. This pilot stopped before full cross-validation.

P2R0F2U.title: Add higher-order Edgeworth terms
P2R0F2U.summary: Check whether the remaining compute budget can support the next Edgeworth correction terms.
P2R0F2U.result: Exact operation counts put every implementable candidate over budget before weight construction. A fifth-order term also lacked the required state. No accuracy experiment ran.

P2R0F3A2.title: Combine analytic and learned corrections
P2R0F3A2.summary: Add an analytic carrier to the estimator while keeping its existing learned correction fixed.
P2R0F3A2.result: MSE was 34% worse than the deployed estimator. The two corrections removed overlapping error twice; comparison only with the uncorrected host had overstated the benefit.

P2R0F3A8.title: Retrain the correction when the estimator changes
P2R0F3A8.summary: Refit the learned correction to features from each changed underlying estimator, rather than reusing an incompatible fit.
P2R0F3A8.result: The tested refits and supplied-feature variants were exhausted. Full-population retraining waits for a new estimator to pass accuracy, stability, and deployment checks.

P2R0F3A6B.title: Supply the trivariate κ211 correction
P2R0F3A6B.summary: Test whether explicit trivariate cumulant terms and related fourth-order corrections improve the deployed estimator.
P2R0F3A6B.result: All five subtests ended without sufficient gain; the remaining terms missed the 2% continuation threshold and deployment economics failed. Higher-order or different state representations remain possible.

P2R0F3B.title: Propagate means without the current approximation
P2R0F3B.summary: Explore backward operators and richer carried state as routes to more exact mean propagation.
P2R0F3B.result: Every specified experiment stopped. The backward route added no new operator, and tested compressed representations failed. Further work requires a new cost certificate or covariance-remainder theorem.

P2R0F3B1A.title: Test backward Hermite propagation
P2R0F3B1A.summary: Compare backward and forward Duhamel propagation, then measure whether cheap higher-order terms add a useful operator.
P2R0F3B1A.result: Forward and reverse agreed to numerical precision. Cheap higher orders failed the improvement and stability tests; the first distinct degree-five basis required over nine trillion coefficients.

P2R0F3B2B5.title: Test a compressed estimator end to end
P2R0F3B2B5.summary: Check whether compressed carried state preserves enough accuracy while satisfying covariance validity and the full compute budget.
P2R0F3B2B5.result: This end-to-end test is blocked. The residual carrier and autonomous stability must first work; no production accuracy or cost result is established here.

P2R0F3B2B2D.title: Bound the error of resetting higher cumulants
P2R0F3B2B2D.summary: Prove a shared positive-semidefinite base and a uniform error bound when converting third- through fifth-order cumulants across 16 layers.
P2R0F3B2B2D.result: The required theorem is still missing. This is a mathematical prerequisite for reopening the reset method, separate from constructing or pricing its state carrier.

P2R0C1D5R1.title: Reduce CP3 cost with nested Winograd arithmetic
P2R0C1D5R1.summary: Use a nested allocation schedule and paired channels to reduce CP3 multiplication cost while preserving numerical output.
P2R0C1D5R1.result: Arithmetic savings and numerical drift passed, but residual runtime exceeded the limit and memory reached 11.95 GB. This implementation stopped after its first candidate.

P2R0C1D9.title: Use one-level Winograd products for cubic moments
P2R0C1D9.summary: Replace the cubic carrier’s large matrix products with one level of Winograd multiplication in reusable scratch memory. The moment formulas stay the same; output differences are limited to floating-point rounding.
P2R0C1D9.result: Submission #328586 passed all 100 grading cases. Adjusted MSE improved 6.94% to 2.125804e−8 while raw MSE stayed effectively unchanged.

P2R0G3.title: Compress hidden state by its effect on the output
P2R0G3.summary: Keep a small set of carrier directions or original columns chosen for their contribution to the final output.
P2R0G3.result: Useful information was too spread out: rank 64 retained under 70% in every tested block, and 2,048-column variants lost accuracy. Synthesizing new Tucker directions remained a separate option.

P2R0G2B.title: Cost of a complete directional state carrier
P2R0G2B.summary: Price the carrier rank needed to preserve the measured effect of hidden state on the final output.
P2R0G2B.result: Even the most favorable shared, layer-specific lower bound exceeded available compute by 39.0 billion FLOPs, before constructing the output action. This carrier could not be deployed.

P2R0G5B.title: Keep 2,048 original CP3 columns
P2R0G5B.summary: Choose existing carrier columns by age, tensor energy, or their estimated effect on the output.
P2R0G5B.result: Every selection rule lost too much accuracy. The best MSE was 2.502645e−7 versus 2.856783e−8 for the full carrier, despite retaining most of the selection proxy’s score.

P2R0G13.title: Carry all 20 native features across layers
P2R0G13.summary: Transport each of the estimator’s 20 standardized features separately and fit a ridge correction from their accumulated history.
P2R0G13.result: The inner test improved by only 0.23%, below the required 1%. The protected test was left unopened; further work needed new joint information rather than more pointwise history.

P2R0C1D11.title: Can the R40 compute schedule beat the deployed score?
P2R0C1D11.summary: Count the physical arithmetic for an R40 schedule that aims to lower compute cost without changing raw error.
P2R0C1D11.result: The schedule’s tensor identity passed, but even an optimistic version with free forward work exceeded break-even cost by 8.88 billion FLOPs. Further savings or an accuracy gain were required.

P2R0C1D13.title: Reuse repeated arithmetic in D4
P2R0C1D13.summary: Eliminate repeated non-matrix-multiplication calculations in the D4 implementation while preserving small-case and reset results.
P2R0C1D13.result: Static counting saved 7.64 billion FLOPs per call and small-case parity passed. The sole full-size official call failed, so the saving was not established as deployable.

P2R0G12B.title: Learn a nonlinear correction from transported history
P2R0G12B.summary: Use the transported 20-feature history in a nonlinear head for late-layer corrections.
P2R0G12B.result: Cross-validation improved 0.403%, with gains in all four folds and on the protected set. This showed useful information, but its underlying estimator still lost to the native model.

P2R0C1D16C.title: D5 submission with an obsolete archive manifest
P2R0C1D16C.summary: Submit the packed D5 estimator and check whether the uploaded archive runs correctly.
P2R0C1D16C.result: Submission #328627 failed generically with an obsolete manifest. The unchanged estimator later ran successfully through official execution, so this failure applies to the archive, not its mathematics.

P2R0C1D22.title: Run D5 through the official client and server
P2R0C1D22.summary: Check that the unchanged D5 estimator can return an output through the official interprocess execution path.
P2R0C1D22.result: After the permission fix, one registered network returned finite output without exception. This established a single successful return, not repeatability or the three-call resource limit.

P2R0F2S0.title: Measure whether the third-order innovation is dense
P2R0F2S0.summary: Build the full-plane third-order innovation without reading targets, then measure how widely its energy is distributed.
P2R0F2S0.result: The probe met source-cost and memory limits, but its energy was overwhelmingly low-rank. It failed the required density test, so training and integration did not proceed.

P2R0G17A.title: Estimate connected sixth-order state from replica paths
P2R0G17A.summary: Use independent difference-replica paths to supply connected sixth-order terms involving at least three coordinates.
P2R0G17A.result: The registered screen found noise far above the allowed signal ratio. The estimated path count needed to pass would cost 7.7 times the entire budget in path multiplications alone.

P2R0G18B5.title: Refit and package the failed cross-validation variant
P2R0G18B5.summary: Refit, export, and package the candidate only if its cross-validation result succeeds.
P2R0G18B5.result: The authenticated scientific result failed. All steps that depended on a pass stopped; their static designs are documentation, not a trained or submitted estimator.

P2R0G18B5D.title: Check refitted-model parity with the generic implementation
P2R0G18B5D.summary: Compare a reviewed refitted model with its generic parent before deployment.
P2R0G18B5D.result: The underlying cross-validation branch failed and produced no reviewed refit model. Parity testing therefore never became applicable.

P2R0G18B5A1.title: Match experiment outputs to the result-sealing format
P2R0G18B5A1.summary: Validate that the post-run recorder can consume the experiment’s exact output fields and preserve an authentic receipt.
P2R0G18B5A1.result: Static review passed, but the live field names disagreed with the experiment’s output. This recorder version was unusable without a revised schema; no live results were inspected.

P2R0G18B5C4.title: Verify that published package bytes match their receipt
P2R0G18B5C4.summary: Test whether the package builder’s recorded hash describes the actual bytes it publishes.
P2R0G18B5C4.result: An adversarial successful write could substitute equal-length bytes without detection. Despite passing 379 earlier cases, this builder stopped before package freeze and required a rehash of actual bytes.

P2R0G18C.title: Test whether the sampled sixth-order source is usable
P2R0G18C.summary: Measure the signal and noise of the proposed sixth-order source under the fixed path budget.
P2R0G18C.result: The science test rejected the source: affordable path counts were too noisy. Earlier scope records remain valid administrative history, but do not establish a useful estimator component.

P2R0G18C3.title: Independently certify the sampled-source test scope
P2R0G18C3.summary: Check that the controller’s chosen roles and metadata obey the fixed experimental scope before downstream use.
P2R0G18C3.result: The source itself failed its scientific test, making this unfinished certification unnecessary for that version. The interrupted recorder remained unreviewed and supplied no evidence.

P2R0G19B_K3SQ.title: Add squared-skewness emission terms
P2R0G19B_K3SQ.summary: Test second-order pairs of third-cumulant terms in both repeated-index planes and fully distinct tensor entries.
P2R0G19B_K3SQ.result: The plane terms improved accuracy and conversion and were enabled. Distinct-entry terms helped at width 256 but slightly hurt at width 1,024, so they stayed disabled there.

P2R0G19B_CARRIER_COMPRESS_NOGO.title: Can the third-order correction be compressed?
P2R0G19B_CARRIER_COMPRESS_NOGO.summary: Try low-rank, collective, star, ridge, permutation, block, and richer-coefficient summaries of the K21 correction.
P2R0G19B_CARRIER_COMPRESS_NOGO.result: All seven tested compression families closed. The useful correction depended on the identities of individual coordinates and was not preserved by these summaries.

P2R0G19B_MATH_REST_IDENTIFIABILITY.title: Determine what quartic moments identify
P2R0G19B_MATH_REST_IDENTIFIABILITY.summary: Organize the separate mathematical questions about quartic moment ambiguity and the unobserved remainder.
P2R0G19B_MATH_REST_IDENTIFIABILITY.result: This entry groups independently testable claims. It has no single result of its own; each child must be resolved on its own evidence.

P2R0G19B_MATH_H3_DAG.title: Determine the shared target-adjoint rank
P2R0G19B_MATH_H3_DAG.summary: Organize the rank questions shared by the NCQC, H3, and q4 target-adjoint calculations.
P2R0G19B_MATH_H3_DAG.result: This entry groups separate mathematical claims rather than reporting one experiment. Results belong to the individual children and do not automatically transfer between them.

P2R0G19B_K31_R55_FIBER_CONTEXT_COUNT.title: Dimension of the moment ambiguity at r55
P2R0G19B_K31_R55_FIBER_CONTEXT_COUNT.summary: Count how many states share the same covariance and K21 moments, and how many additional contexts can distinguish them generically.
P2R0G19B_K31_R55_FIBER_CONTEXT_COUNT.result: The proposed dimension count is 2,099, but the joint symmetric/stabilizer condition remains unproved. Separate generic block arguments do not establish the exact fiber size, conditioning, or numerical accuracy.

P2R0G19B_K31_MOMENT_INTERFACE.title: Does total K31 provide new information?
P2R0G19B_K31_MOMENT_INTERFACE.summary: Check whether a cheap exact oracle for the same-site K31 action would supply a feature missing from the estimator.
P2R0G19B_K31_MOMENT_INTERFACE.result: The total action was already present in D11/Q24. Computing it again could help implementation or auditing, but could not provide a new correction source.

P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_REVERSE_COST.title: Cost of a reverse K31 contraction
P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_REVERSE_COST.summary: Factor the AQ reverse contraction and reuse masks to compute the same-site K31 feature cheaply.
P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_REVERSE_COST.result: The contraction can be cheap, but exact subtraction of the existing D11 contribution leaves no new same-site feature. Lower cost does not create an accuracy contribution.

P2R0G19B_K31_HGE3_TAIL.title: Bound the higher-order tail beyond the AQ approximation
P2R0G19B_K31_HGE3_TAIL.summary: Account for higher Hermite orders and errors in the frame, state, and masks that the AQ approximation omits.
P2R0G19B_K31_HGE3_TAIL.result: Current second-moment bounds do not control the fourth-moment tail needed for ReLU. A weighted bound below 3.80e−6, or proof that an extra exact action is necessary, remains open.

P2R0G19B_K31_OLDSPAN_LEDGER.title: Account for K31 terms already in the estimator
P2R0G19B_K31_OLDSPAN_LEDGER.summary: Trace every same-layer fourth-order and K31 contribution through CP4, covariance pairing, star, and H31 terms.
P2R0G19B_K31_OLDSPAN_LEDGER.result: The audit identified all existing contributions. A proposed new correction must subtract this complete baseline to avoid counting the same action twice.

P2R0G19B_K31_SAME_SITE_D11_DUPLICATE.title: Prove the same-site K31 action is already included
P2R0G19B_K31_SAME_SITE_D11_DUPLICATE.summary: Match the location, centering, off-diagonal mask, and evaluation order of K31 against the estimator’s assembled terms.
P2R0G19B_K31_SAME_SITE_D11_DUPLICATE.result: The exact trace and adjoint identity show that total K31 equals the existing CP4, star, and H31 action. Adding it again would duplicate the contribution.

P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_STRICT_DEPTH_THEOREM.title: When can a correction across layers be new?
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_STRICT_DEPTH_THEOREM.summary: Distinguish a new cross-layer effect from an action already generated by the estimator’s existing operators.
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_STRICT_DEPTH_THEOREM.result: The forward/reverse identity permits novelty only across strictly different depths after removing the complete existing operator span. Same-site actions are duplicates.

P2R0G19B_OFFDIAG_Q211_INDEPENDENT_SOURCE.title: Fourth-order interactions not fixed by lower moments
P2R0G19B_OFFDIAG_Q211_INDEPENDENT_SOURCE.summary: Construct distributions with identical lower moments and marginal or pairwise fourth-order information but different three-variable fourth cumulants.
P2R0G19B_OFFDIAG_Q211_INDEPENDENT_SOURCE.result: An exact seven-leaf construction changes κ4(A,A,B,C) while preserving all those other measurements. This proves that the off-diagonal interaction can contain independent information.

P2R0G19B_H6_H8_ANALYTIC_FOLD.title: Contract sixth- and eighth-order terms without storing them
P2R0G19B_H6_H8_ANALYTIC_FOLD.summary: Use analytic contractions to pass from fourth order through sixth and eighth order and back, avoiding large stored tensors.
P2R0G19B_H6_H8_ANALYTIC_FOLD.result: The identities remove storage, but synchronized products and intervening weights still cost work. A fused computation within budget and an endpoint error bound remain unproved.

P2R0G19B_GENERIC_Q211_RANK_NOGO.title: Can the q211 state share one direction?
P2R0G19B_GENERIC_Q211_RANK_NOGO.summary: Test whether dense ReLU resets let the required fourth-order interactions collapse onto a common rank-one direction.
P2R0G19B_GENERIC_Q211_RANK_NOGO.result: Generically they do not: resets create independent Hermite and Jordan directions. Only separately proved invariant or output-invisible exceptions could justify rank one.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_H4_RESIDUAL_SUFFIX.title: Carry the discarded fourth-order residual plane
P2R0G19B_NCQC_H4_RESIDUAL_SUFFIX.summary: Retain the positive-semidefinite part discarded by the AQ reset to recover missing fourth-order energy and sign.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_H4_RESIDUAL_SUFFIX.result: This remains a proposal. It needs proof that the contribution is new, affordable to reset and combine, stable under repeated use, and useful at the output.

P2R0G19B_AD2_DEPLOY_PROVENANCE.title: Match the analytic source to the deployed fourth-order action
P2R0G19B_AD2_DEPLOY_PROVENANCE.summary: Check that the analytic tree source includes every fourth-order face and producer change that matters to the deployed output.
P2R0G19B_AD2_DEPLOY_PROVENANCE.result: The required output-weighted error bound is still missing. It must support retention of at least 0.95696 after subtracting the estimator’s existing contributions.

P2R0G19B_AK_SHARED_REVERSE_48.title: Share reverse work across fourth-order corrections
P2R0G19B_AK_SHARED_REVERSE_48.summary: Combine one reverse calculation with complete distinct-index and local quartic actions, aiming for a total of 48 products.
P2R0G19B_AK_SHARED_REVERSE_48.result: The count is conditional on complete sources at the same boundary. Provenance, factorization, mixed-order closure, terminal coverage, and a positive net replacement gain remain to be proved.

P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_STAR_PAIR_RANK2.title: Rank of a restricted three-variable quartic correction
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_STAR_PAIR_RANK2.summary: Remove the matching star and pairing terms from the K22 plane restricted to three variables.
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_STAR_PAIR_RANK2.result: The remaining signed CP representation has exact rank two; rank one is impossible. This local result does not justify a single global pairing-scalar update.

P2R0G19B_Q211_NATIVE_P_RESIDENCY.title: Reuse the ordered-product buffer exactly
P2R0G19B_Q211_NATIVE_P_RESIDENCY.summary: Avoid rebuilding an ordered product by reusing the identical product already computed for the signed third-order action.
P2R0G19B_Q211_NATIVE_P_RESIDENCY.result: Building it afresh exceeds the intended cost. The required proof must identify the same buffer, factor convention, and lifetime on every active layer; that reuse is not yet established.

P2R0G19B_AQ_TILT_FUTURE_DARK_GATE.title: Can discarded state affect future outputs?
P2R0G19B_AQ_TILT_FUTURE_DARK_GATE.summary: Check whether information outside the carried AQ observation stays invisible after all later ReLU resets.
P2R0G19B_AQ_TILT_FUTURE_DARK_GATE.result: A bounded-rank reverse calculation is valid only if future pullbacks annihilate that missing information, or its coherent output effect fits the error allowance. That proof remains open.

P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_VALUE.title: Measure the output gain of a four-direction repair
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_VALUE.summary: Apply a local fourth-order repair at the final transition and count only the contribution absent from the existing estimator.
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_VALUE.result: A legal local repair is not yet an accuracy result. It still needs the prescribed action tests, joint channel accounting, and at least 2.86e−10 gain.

P2R0G19B_AQ_Q211_RESIDUAL_ARITY.title: Decompose the missing fourth-cumulant terms
P2R0G19B_AQ_Q211_RESIDUAL_ARITY.summary: Expand the fourth-cumulant difference by how many argument slots contain a residual.
P2R0G19B_AQ_Q211_RESIDUAL_ARITY.result: The exact expansion has multiplicities 4, 6, 4, and 1. A one-variable tilted generator covers only part of it; terms with multiple residuals need joint observations or a fourth-moment bound.

P2R0G19B_AQ_AFFINE_Q211_ALL_CHAOS_JET.title: Second-order correlation expansion for biased ReLU
P2R0G19B_AQ_AFFINE_Q211_ALL_CHAOS_JET.summary: Use Price derivatives to sum all Hermite orders through quadratic order in off-diagonal correlations, including arbitrary biases.
P2R0G19B_AQ_AFFINE_Q211_ALL_CHAOS_JET.result: The algebra is exact through correlation order two and matches the centered fourth-order formula at zero bias. Deployment still needs a cheap query and a bound on the remaining higher orders.

P2R0G19B_R54_ACTUAL_SECTION_RECEIPT.title: Conditioning of the r54 representation near the affine limit
P2R0G19B_R54_ACTUAL_SECTION_RECEIPT.summary: Analyze the Jacobian after removing gauge and parity freedoms to see whether the proposed moment representation can be inverted reliably.
P2R0G19B_R54_ACTUAL_SECTION_RECEIPT.result: At least 51,341 modes are absent at first order, implying conditioning at least as bad as t⁻³ near the affine limit. Cubic rank and usable finite-scale conditioning remain unproved.

P2R0G19B_AQ_LOW_GRAM_PUSH_CSE_NOGO.title: Transporting features does not compute their pairwise Gram
P2R0G19B_AQ_LOW_GRAM_PUSH_CSE_NOGO.summary: Check whether the transported feature matrix already supplies the pairwise inner products needed by the AQ method.
P2R0G19B_AQ_LOW_GRAM_PUSH_CSE_NOGO.result: It does not: the Gram matrix is a separate generic product, and marginal spectra lose relative orientations. The proposed cost count fails without an existing buffer or an exact fused product.

P2R0G19B_AQ_FROZEN_GREST_FRAME_LIPSCHITZ.title: Sensitivity of the Gaussian higher-order remainder
P2R0G19B_AQ_FROZEN_GREST_FRAME_LIPSCHITZ.summary: Bound how much the Gaussian remainder covariance changes when correlations change while marginal distributions stay fixed.
P2R0G19B_AQ_FROZEN_GREST_FRAME_LIPSCHITZ.result: The exact Lipschitz coefficient is at most 1/4 − 1/(2π), about 0.090845, for every bias. This does not bound marginal drift, non-Gaussian errors, or accumulation through later layers.

P2R0G19B_Q211_AABC_PARTITION_INTERTWINER.title: A q211 mask is not preserved by dense transport
P2R0G19B_Q211_AABC_PARTITION_INTERTWINER.summary: Check whether isolating the 2–1–1 index pattern before a weight transformation gives the same result as isolating it afterward.
P2R0G19B_Q211_AABC_PARTITION_INTERTWINER.result: The operations do not commute. A carrier for that pattern alone is invalid unless it also supplies exact compensation for all the other collision patterns.

P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SUFFIX_COST.title: Count the cost of six AQ55 resets
P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SUFFIX_COST.summary: Count paid Gram products for a six-reset suffix, including the option of switching to exact total covariance at the endpoint.
P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SUFFIX_COST.result: Under the stated conventions, the switch costs 46.640 product equivalents and leaves 2.360. This arithmetic excludes unresolved source, representation, and stabilization costs.

P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_Q211_PAIR_MINUS_TRACE.title: The missing trace term in the quadratic q211 formula
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_Q211_PAIR_MINUS_TRACE.summary: Use Price’s identity at zero bias to separate the quadratic fourth-order action into pairing and trace contributions.
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_Q211_PAIR_MINUS_TRACE.result: The exact formula identifies a missing trace lift relative to the carried approximation. It adds no new source if the complete connected fourth-order surface is already computed.

P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_SECTION_THRESHO.title: Minimum rank for first-order AQ feasibility
P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_SECTION_THRESHO.summary: Count the available degrees of freedom in a first-order AQ representation and compare them with the 2,048 required constraints.
P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_SECTION_THRESHO.result: Rank 63 is the first to pass the dimension count. This establishes a necessary threshold and cost count, not an invertible actual Jacobian or a working initializer.

P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_LOW_RANK_BELLMAN_FUSIO.title: Contract the Stein discrepancy with a low-rank mask
P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_LOW_RANK_BELLMAN_FUSIO.summary: Derive the work needed when the output-relevant mask is supplied as a deterministic rank-k factorization.
P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_LOW_RANK_BELLMAN_FUSIO.result: The algebra gives an exact contraction and cost formula conditional on that mask. It does not establish a low-rank ReLU mask or show that the needed intermediate arrays already exist.

P2R0G19B_R63_PHYSICAL_DEFECT_LOW_RANK_WA.title: Low-rank defects invalidate a coarse r63 shortcut
P2R0G19B_R63_PHYSICAL_DEFECT_LOW_RANK_WA.summary: Check whether every nonzero defect has enough row rank to apply a simple sufficient condition for the r63 representation.
P2R0G19B_R63_PHYSICAL_DEFECT_LOW_RANK_WA.result: Third-moment stabilizers create defects of row rank at most 125, so the rank-176 shortcut fails. The exact stratified test or actual Gram matrix could still succeed.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_LATE_SUFFIX_VALUE_GATE.title: Can a late AQ63 correction reach the accuracy target?
P2R0G19B_AQ63_LATE_SUFFIX_VALUE_GATE.summary: Compare the available late-layer contribution with the amplification needed to bring raw MSE below 1e−8.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_LATE_SUFFIX_VALUE_GATE.result: The recorded contributions require roughly 4.4–4.8 times amplification. Four resets cannot suffice under nonexpansive coupling; a valid high-gain mechanism and tighter error bounds remain missing.

P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SECTION_CONDITIONING_.title: Is the r62 inverse numerically stable?
P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SECTION_CONDITIONING_.summary: Measure the size of the weak singular directions, rather than relying only on a nonzero determinant.
P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SECTION_CONDITIONING_.result: The final 561 singular values scale cubically near the affine limit. Their size, fifth-order drift, and resulting output displacement still need bounds at the actual operating point.

P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_CURRENT_TAP.title: Existing CP4 factors do not supply the reverse query
P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_CURRENT_TAP.summary: Compare the estimator’s forward CP4 factors with the quartic reverse factors required by the output-specific query.
P2R0G19B_PRICE_SHARED_WARING_CURRENT_TAP.result: They represent different objects. Collision projection can also increase rank sharply, so free reuse is unjustified without an exact factorization at the same layer boundary.

P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_CP3_Q4_FUSED_V1.title: Fuse CP3 and quartic features for a q211 correction
P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_CP3_Q4_FUSED_V1.summary: Reduce the affine q211 correction through correlation degree four to matrix-vector and sandwich operations usable as learned features.
P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_CP3_Q4_FUSED_V1.result: This is a candidate feature construction, not an exact residual repair. It still needs bias handling, existing-term subtraction, tail bounds, an affordable output action, and held-out improvement.

P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_D10_REVERSE_REUSE_TAIL.title: Bound the Hermite tail after subtracting existing terms
P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_D10_REVERSE_REUSE_TAIL.summary: Remove already-accounted-for Hermite bands through degree five and bound what remains.
P2R0G19B_AQ_STEIN_D10_REVERSE_REUSE_TAIL.result: The uniform off-diagonal bound starts at degree six and is at most μ⁶/4; centered parity improves the order. This mathematical bound does not prove the required reverse factors are reusable.

P2R0G19B_AQ_SCALAR_ORACLE_ENDPOINT_VALUE.title: Does a scalar AQ oracle improve the final estimate?
P2R0G19B_AQ_SCALAR_ORACLE_ENDPOINT_VALUE.summary: Test whether exact marginal reset moments provide a new cross-unit correction relevant to the output.
P2R0G19B_AQ_SCALAR_ORACLE_ENDPOINT_VALUE.result: Marginal accuracy alone is insufficient. A legal output action must remove existing Q24, CP3, and CP4 contributions and demonstrate additional predictive value; otherwise the oracle remains diagnostic.

P2R0G19B_AQ_FREE_CUMULANT_STAR_DECOMPOSI.title: Decompose free-cumulant errors into star tensors
P2R0G19B_AQ_FREE_CUMULANT_STAR_DECOMPOSI.summary: Derive how third moments and fourth free cumulants transform when freely independent source components are mixed by the weight matrix.
P2R0G19B_AQ_FREE_CUMULANT_STAR_DECOMPOSI.result: The cubic and quartic terms become diagonal CP3 and CP4 star tensors, with a cheap remaining pair term. These exact terms may already be present in a synchronized estimator.

P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_FLATTEN_RANK_THEORE.title: Lower bound on direct fourth-order query count
P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_FLATTEN_RANK_THEORE.summary: Flatten the corrected fourth-order target into paired indices and count how much rank each direct query can represent.
P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_FLATTEN_RANK_THEORE.result: Each direct H211 query contributes rank one in that flattening. Its rank therefore gives an exact lower bound on query count, with further factorization constraints still applying.

P2R0G19B_DENSE_REVERSE_ECONOMIC_REOPEN.title: Reassess the cost of dense reverse calculations
P2R0G19B_DENSE_REVERSE_ECONOMIC_REOPEN.summary: Use measured float32 billing to compare a dense reverse correction’s compute cost with the accuracy it could provide.
P2R0G19B_DENSE_REVERSE_ECONOMIC_REOPEN.result: The corrected accounting shows that 10–20 products are not automatically uneconomic. It supplies no new source or deployable query; raw accuracy must be established first.

P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_PSD_SYNC_GATE.title: Keep the radial approximation covariance valid
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_PSD_SYNC_GATE.summary: Check that the residual covariance stays positive semidefinite both before and after every radial AQ reset.
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_PSD_SYNC_GATE.result: Validity at every active layer remains to be certified. If rescaling is needed, it changes the connected amplitude and the fitted law, so its accuracy cost must also be counted.

P2R0G19B_R62_RANKONE_ANCHOR_UNIVERSALITY.title: A counterexample to a universal r62 obstruction
P2R0G19B_R62_RANKONE_ANCHOR_UNIVERSALITY.summary: Construct a regular non-affine case to test whether an anchor always removes the same cubic information.
P2R0G19B_R62_RANKONE_ANCHOR_UNIVERSALITY.result: An exact rank-one null mode violates the proposed universal claim. Non-affine or overlapping r62 constructions remain possible, but still require the full 561-row Gram test.

P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_COMPRESSED_GRAM_RECE.title: Test the r63 representation at the deployed layer boundary
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_COMPRESSED_GRAM_RECE.summary: Build the output-specific Gram matrix after removing existing estimator contributions, using the actual deployed prefix.
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_COMPRESSED_GRAM_RECE.result: No actual target basis, prefix, singular-value floor, or valid representation radius has been supplied. Those measurements and their acquisition cost remain prerequisites.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_BIPARTITE_CUBIC_NULL_SHORT.title: The bipartite cubic-null construction is too small
P2R0G19B_AQ63_BIPARTITE_CUBIC_NULL_SHORT.summary: Count the usable directions in the largest bipartite construction at rank 63.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_BIPARTITE_CUBIC_NULL_SHORT.result: Its 992 directions fall short of the 1,023 needed for strict projected evaluation and the 1,024 needed for the full target. A larger construction would require exceptional spectral structure.

P2R0G19B_Q24_DEPLOYED_EDGEWORTH_ORDER_AU.title: Which Edgeworth terms does Q24 actually contain?
P2R0G19B_Q24_DEPLOYED_EDGEWORTH_ORDER_AU.summary: Read the deployed density reset to distinguish correlation-series length from the order of cumulants it includes.
P2R0G19B_Q24_DEPLOYED_EDGEWORTH_ORDER_AU.result: The reset contains exactly 1 + L3 + L4 + L3²/2. Its seven Q24 terms are Gaussian Mehler powers, not seven cumulant orders; higher mixed terms are absent.

P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_POSITIVITY.title: Does the completed Edgeworth approximation define a valid law?
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_POSITIVITY.summary: Check positivity and bound the remaining error after adding the proposed higher-order completion.
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_POSITIVITY.result: A finite Edgeworth polynomial need not stay positive. Diffuse order counting supplies no adequate remainder bound; a valid moment/action method or resummation still needs certification at the actual state sizes.

P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_VS_DISJOINT_SCALE_S.title: Shared Gaussian inputs change the AQ tail
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_VS_DISJOINT_SCALE_S.summary: Compare an AQ model whose affine and quadratic terms share Gaussian inputs with a model using disjoint input blocks.
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_VS_DISJOINT_SCALE_S.result: The Gaussian scale-mixture identity holds only for disjoint blocks. Shared inputs add a mixed term of the same leading order, so the claimed rank-one tail collapse does not apply there.

P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_BIRTH_QUOTIE.title: A strict trace term survives collision-only subtraction
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_BIRTH_QUOTIE.summary: Construct a fourth-order trace contribution with zero marginal and pairwise collision faces but nonzero strict q211 entries.
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_BIRTH_QUOTIE.result: The exact construction cannot be removed by collision-only baseline reads. Matching it to the physical leading error still requires the complete pairing comparison; other full trace reads may already include it.

P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_TYPED_READOUT_OWNERS.title: A covariance-derived trace can be a new readout, not a new source
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_TYPED_READOUT_OWNERS.summary: Check whether the nonlinear trace feature is absent from the estimator’s existing response and derivative span.
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_TYPED_READOUT_OWNERS.result: The feature is fully determined by covariance already in memory. It adds no source information; only a synchronized residual test can establish a useful new way of reading that information.

P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_COSTATE_LEAF_RANK_.title: A rank-one output mask can require full source support
P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_COSTATE_LEAF_RANK_.summary: Derive the physical q211 source support required by a rank-one downstream covariance mask under a dense invertible weight matrix.
P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_COSTATE_LEAF_RANK_.result: The resulting source matrix is generically full rank. A rank-one downstream mask therefore does not justify a low-rank physical q211 query.

P2R0G19B_Q211_STRUCTURED_LEAF_COLLISION_.title: Account for excluded collision terms in cheap contractions
P2R0G19B_Q211_STRUCTURED_LEAF_COLLISION_.summary: Check whether one- or two-product formulas remain valid when strict source exclusions remove collision entries.
P2R0G19B_Q211_STRUCTURED_LEAF_COLLISION_.result: The cheap formulas assume completed source planes. Their collision rows, normalization, and buffer lifetimes must already be present at the same layer boundary, or their full cost and residual effect must be added.

P2R0G19B_R55_FIBER_2099_GATE.title: Verify the claimed 2,099-dimensional r55 ambiguity
P2R0G19B_R55_FIBER_2099_GATE.summary: Test the joint symmetric and stabilizer constraints required for the advertised fiber dimension.
P2R0G19B_R55_FIBER_2099_GATE.result: The exact count remains conditional on one joint minor or Schur test. Separate generic block witnesses do not prove that all the required conditions hold together.

P2R0G19B_STATE_ESTIMATION_FRONTIER.title: Can learned physical state justify further integration?
P2R0G19B_STATE_ESTIMATION_FRONTIER.summary: After local correction providers failed, retain one small nine-fit model test on a previously examined network.
P2R0G19B_STATE_ESTIMATION_FRONTIER.result: The remaining check is descriptive: raw MSE below 1e−8 could justify reviewing integration. It would not establish fresh held-out accuracy or authorize packaging; the fresh-test infrastructure stayed paused.

P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RUNNER_ARCHIT.title: Add four inputs to the correction network
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RUNNER_ARCHIT.summary: Extend the unchanged 82-input correction model with four new fields while keeping the specified shared hidden layers and six outputs.
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RUNNER_ARCHIT.result: Static inspection confirmed 86 inputs, three 256-unit SiLU layers, six scalar heads, and 155,398 parameters. This verifies architecture, not estimator accuracy.

P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_FOLD0_SENTINE.title: Do four extra fields improve the correction?
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_FOLD0_SENTINE.summary: Compare the correction with the four new fields enabled and zeroed in one fixed cross-validation fold.
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_FOLD0_SENTINE.result: The fields changed MSE only slightly, recovering 0.0935% of the parent-to-oracle gap against an 8% requirement. The one-shot test failed and the remaining folds were not run.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_PROTOCOL.title: Prepare a fresh test with independent reference streams
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_PROTOCOL.summary: Preserve a test design that selects the network without targets and separates reference streams to control evaluation noise and leakage.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_PROTOCOL.result: The protocol remained paused and accessed no data. Work could resume only after the descriptive test passed and a separate review; fresh targets would not open automatically.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.title: Test a nine-fit state model on an exposed network
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.summary: Freeze a small physical-state model and compare its final-layer error with the source enabled and disabled on one already-examined network.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.result: Three static audits passed, but the recorded claim reports no run or result. Because this network was already exposed, even a pass would be descriptive evidence, not a fresh held-out test.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_G3_COFIRE_PACKAGE.title: Combine third-order supply with a cheaper float32 package
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_G3_COFIRE_PACKAGE.summary: Try to turn measured third-order corrections, refits, and compute savings into a candidate that improves the deployed adjusted score.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_G3_COFIRE_PACKAGE.result: The measured correction routes did not beat the existing submission. Only the float32 package was ready, with unchanged raw error and 4.9% lower adjusted cost; no new submission was made.

P2R0G19B_PKG_WALL_RETRACTED.title: Correct an overstated third-order compute barrier
P2R0G19B_PKG_WALL_RETRACTED.summary: Recheck whether useful third-order corrections truly require an unaffordable dense tensor, and examine how the corrections are consumed.
P2R0G19B_PKG_WALL_RETRACTED.result: The earlier impossibility reading was retracted: truncation tests had broken cancellations. Useful value largely came from second-order path terms already carried; the remaining mismatch was in plane calculations.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_VCHANNEL.title: Correct the variance error carried between layers
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_VCHANNEL.summary: Use the propagated covariance error to correct each next-layer variance, and measure how much final error that channel can remove.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_VCHANNEL.result: Independent-reference scoring showed a real but smaller benefit than the original same-sample estimate. Much of the apparent gain was noise matching; useful variance error was concentrated in layers 8–15.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2D_FOURTH.title: Test exact fourth-order inputs to the emission step
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2D_FOURTH.summary: Replace the carried K22 and K31 planes with reference values to learn which downstream correction they limit.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2D_FOURTH.result: Exact fourth-order inputs did not improve the variance correction, but did improve the fourth-cumulant channel and the joint result. They were therefore not the variance bottleneck.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N4_F2J.title: Explain and refit the learned residual correction
P2R0G19B_MECH_N4_F2J.summary: Measure what the deployed learned correction fixes, then refit it after mechanistic variance and higher-moment changes.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N4_F2J.result: Refits on the modified estimators failed to beat deployment. Analysis linked 84% of the original correction to the fourth-order plane defect; reusing the old fit after state fixes over-corrected errors.

P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB6_VIRGIN_GATE.title: Prepare a six-network fresh evaluation
P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB6_VIRGIN_GATE.summary: Build a full-size test harness with independent reference means, the deployed baseline, and the actual compute budget before any new submission.
P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB6_VIRGIN_GATE.result: The harness was ready, but no candidate earned entry by beating the prior tests and adjusted-score target. No candidate was submitted through this route.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_II_PUSH.title: Recover fourth-order information lost during transport
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_II_PUSH.summary: Trace the missing K22 and K31 content when fourth-order state passes through a weight matrix, and test cheaper ways to carry it.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_II_PUSH.result: Cheap block terms recovered only about 1% of the missing content, and larger CP4 ranks did not fix it. The available plane-chain repair overlapped the learned correction; the wider transport problem remained unresolved.

P2R0E3A0.title: Frozen CP3 benchmark and conditional Gaussian comparison
P2R0E3A0.summary: Keep the accepted CP3 result as the control, with a Gaussian comparison on the same underlying estimator only if the preceding accuracy tests qualified.
P2R0E3A0.result: The benchmark was accepted. The preceding tests failed, so the conditional Gaussian comparison was never run.

P2R0E3A6.title: Reducing the Hermite expansion from order 32 to 24
P2R0E3A6.summary: Keep all 17 correction channels while reducing the Hermite/rho expansion from order 32 to 24; test numerical agreement, cost, and final accuracy.
P2R0E3A6.result: Order 24 passed all 100 operational tests, but final MSE was 5.765125013112993e-7, above 1e-8. Three tiny disagreements with order 32 did not prove general equivalence. A separate float32 order-32 variant was unstable.

P2R0H3B.title: Gaussian fallback for negative third or fourth moments
P2R0H3B.summary: Replace a propagated moment tuple with Gaussian positive-part moments whenever its third or fourth raw moment becomes negative.
P2R0H3B.result: The fallback recovered two failures but made three previously finite cases nonfinite and caused one enormous prediction change. This exact trigger and replacement were rejected.

P2R0H3H.title: A tolerant check at the variance floor
P2R0H3H.summary: Check whether variance is within twice the numerical floor, instead of testing exact equality, before normalizing correlations.
P2R0H3H.result: Three rounding-edge cases escaped the equality check and amplified tiny denominators. The relaxed check repaired all three, returning their errors to ordinary e-8 levels while preserving the normal branch.

P2R0H7A.title: Fit a learned correction to the estimator’s own outputs
P2R0H7A.summary: Train a learned correction on features from the third- and fourth-moment estimator’s own trajectory. Apply the correction after propagation, then compare complete predictions on 40 protected networks.
P2R0H7A.result: All 40 networks improved with finite predictions. Validation MSE was 3.1072e-8, about 35% of the uncorrected result. Submission #328317 then recorded raw MSE 3.1162e-8; the full-data upgrade is a separate experiment.

P2R0F2E.title: Training the residual model on its own predictions
P2R0F2E.summary: Train a 6,688-parameter residual-state model while exposing it to errors from its own rollout, rather than supplying correct intermediate states throughout.
P2R0F2E.result: Autonomous MSE improved to 3.4710e-8 but missed the preregistered 3.44e-8 target. With correct intermediate states it reached 8.2080e-9, leaving a 4.23-fold gap. This training schedule was stopped.

P2R0F2K.title: Adding pooled Gram-matrix context to the residual model
P2R0F2K.summary: Use full Gram-matrix context across all 688 training networks and measure predictions on folds excluded from their model fits.
P2R0F2K.result: Out-of-fold MSE was 3.2444e-8, 0.34% worse than model J. Both the average-error and worst-network targets failed, so no deployment measurement followed.

P2R0C1A.title: How much compute reduction could improve the score?
P2R0C1A.summary: Use submission #328586 to calculate the tradeoff between raw prediction error and the compute multiplier in the adjusted score.
P2R0C1A.result: At unchanged raw MSE, beating 7.70e-9 adjusted would require a multiplier below 0.261823, equivalent to at most about 5.758e11 FLOPs at constant cost. The bound changes with the estimator and per-network scoring.

P2R0C1D4.title: Correcting layer one in a rank-16,384 CP3 model
P2R0C1D4.summary: Seed the dynamic state with a learned first-layer correction, then test whether that improvement survives propagation to the final layer.
P2R0C1D4.result: All 40 rollouts were finite, but MSE was 7.3517e-7, 20.77 times the cost-derived target. The layer-one gain decayed sharply with depth; later state propagation remained the limitation.

P2R0F2V.title: Removing an unnecessary covariance eigendecomposition
P2R0F2V.summary: Measure which parts of the estimator consume substantial compute without materially improving accuracy, starting with the unconditional covariance repair.
P2R0F2V.result: Removing the eigendecomposition succeeded in submission #328439: raw MSE 2.9409e-8 and adjusted 2.2843e-8. A conditional Cholesky replacement had failed. CP3 computation remained necessary.

P2R0F3A3.title: Lower-cost CP3 execution with unchanged prediction error
P2R0F3A3.summary: Reduce the cost of CP3 computation through successive submitted implementations while checking that prediction accuracy is preserved.
P2R0F3A3.result: Submission #328586 reached adjusted MSE 2.1258043e-8, a 6.94% improvement over #328439. Raw MSE changed by only 5.47e-14. Further safe reductions had been measured out.

P2R0F3A8A.title: Retraining the learned correction after changing its base estimator
P2R0F3A8A.summary: Refit, export, and integrate the correction for the modified base estimator, then evaluate it in the form actually used for prediction.
P2R0F3A8A.result: The pipeline worked end to end, but even the optimistic in-sample adjusted projection was 2.833e-8, worse than the 2.2843e-8 benchmark. The infrastructure passed; this estimator change did not improve the result.

P2R0F3A6B1.title: Matching third-order pair and marginal corrections
P2R0F3A6B1.summary: Add the matching third-order terms to both pair and marginal formulas, then test whether their previous order mismatch caused the loss.
P2R0F3A6B1.result: The formulas were verified, but matched corrections worsened MSE by 2.85%; half amplitude worsened it by 1.36%. These valid comparisons rejected the retrofit. A separate univariate-only result used a mismatched learned correction.

P2R0F3B1.title: Propagating Hermite corrections backward from the output
P2R0F3B1.summary: Compare backward contraction with forward correction propagation, and test whether a richer backward basis adds useful accuracy at legal cost.
P2R0F3B1.result: For fixed sources the two directions agreed to 1.93e-16. The tested degree ladder failed its accuracy requirements; a literal full degree-five basis exceeded the entire compute budget before transport. Structured alternatives remain separate.

P2R0F3B1B.title: A structured fifth-order correction for the requested output
P2R0F3B1B.summary: Seek a fused representation of the missing [311] and [221] fifth-order sources, rather than repeating the equivalent fixed-source backward computation.
P2R0F3B1B.result: Blocked pending an explicit structured construction. Generic contraction alone costs about 14.96 times the full budget; a candidate needs verified source terms, small-width agreement, and a fully priced rank-13 or cheaper circuit.

P2R0F3B1B1.title: Why fixed-source backward fifth-order contraction adds no operator
P2R0F3B1B1.summary: Audit whether reversing a fixed fifth-order source creates a new correction, and price the distinct source that the original computation lacks.
P2R0F3B1B1.result: The reverse computation is exactly the forward Duhamel correction. The genuinely different [311]+[221] source costs about 3.289e13 FLOPs to contract generically, before constructing it. This implementation was closed.

P2R0F3B2B3A.title: The query cost of a generic rank-16 TT cumulant state
P2R0F3B2B3A.summary: Price several ways of reading a rank-16 TT state, including shared prefixes and an optimistic varying-fiber computation.
P2R0F3B2B3A.result: The cheapest estimate was 61,440 operations per query, above the absolute integrated ceiling of 9,935 before response work. A materially different fused representation would need its own cost proof.

P2R0C1D6.title: Preallocating a sequential Winograd computation
P2R0C1D6.summary: Remove streaming allocation and reuse a fixed arena for sequential channels, then test the runtime overhead on a small exact-runtime case.
P2R0C1D6.result: Arithmetic, aliasing, cost, and tiny byte parity passed. Runtime overhead was 49.6 ms against a 10 ms limit, due to 6,786 Python records in the hot path. Full-size execution was therefore skipped.

P2R0C1D9H.title: Combining a cheaper CP3 push with direct reads
P2R0C1D9H.summary: Keep the depth-one implementation’s cheaper propagation while restoring direct reads of the resulting state.
P2R0C1D9H.result: Output and operation-count checks passed, but the local residual runtime was 0.43475 seconds. The fixed candidate failed its runtime test and was stopped without retry.

P2R0G4.title: Stacking re-anchoring with an analytic continuation
P2R0G4.summary: Combine directional re-anchoring, covariance resummation, and an output-sensitive correction on the existing depth-one estimator.
P2R0G4.result: The individual rank-13 pieces were affordable, but the required output-sensitive state was too diffuse. The higher-rank lower bound exceeded available compute by 39.0 billion FLOPs. No candidate was launched.

P2R0G3A.title: How many directions does the output-sensitive state need?
P2R0G3A.summary: Measure the spectrum of local correction sources across six layers on three networks, including mixed higher-order terms.
P2R0G3A.result: The best 13 directions captured far less than the required 70% of relevant energy. This source-only screen rejected the proposed compact state before any estimator or protected target was opened.

P2R0G5C.title: Compressing CP3 with Tucker and hierarchical tensor factors
P2R0G5C.summary: Test whether a more expressive hierarchical tensor reconstruction could retain the teacher’s useful state within the proposed lower compute budget.
P2R0G5C.result: Even the favorable teacher-capacity test gave MSE 6.7735e-8 against a 3.0606e-8 target. The unprojected control also failed. The reconstruction was stopped before autonomous implementation.

P2R0G14.title: Fine-tuning the existing q predictor for final-layer error
P2R0G14.summary: Optimize the same 6,022 parameters and unchanged input features against autonomous final-layer prediction error.
P2R0G14.result: The best epoch improved MSE by only 0.117%, short of the required 1%. The protected validation set stayed unopened. Further work needed a new information source, rather than another fit of these features.

P2R0G11C.title: Cancelled CP4-cap tests on a failed base estimator
P2R0G11C.summary: Plan a larger validation panel for CP4 capacity reductions added to the G11B estimator.
P2R0G11C.result: A submission failure invalidated the base estimator before this panel ran. No target-free calls, targets, output directories, or submission were created. Tests on the separate plain depth-one estimator were tracked elsewhere.

P2R0C1D14.title: Increasing the exact computation-arena depth
P2R0C1D14.summary: Test deeper exact arena implementations under the official resource limits and submit the variants that pass.
P2R0C1D14.result: Depths three and four passed and received scores; depth four became submission #328622. The original memory-heavy depth-five form failed. Its later packed implementation and remote failures are separate records.

P2R0G12C8.title: Learning an autonomous suffix state with exact weights
P2R0G12C8.summary: Train the first exact-weight suffix-state model from scratch and compare it with the native estimator and nonlinear-Z model across four held-out folds.
P2R0G12C8.result: It improved none of the four folds. Pooled MSE was 3.1215e-8, worse than nonlinear-Z at 3.0538e-8 and native at 2.9737e-8. This first version was stopped without export or retry.

P2R0C1D16D.title: Testing packed depth-five execution in the official runtime
P2R0C1D16D.summary: Run the packaged depth-five source both locally and through the official client/server path, including repeat calls in one persistent process.
P2R0C1D16D.result: Calls, operation counts, finite outputs, repeatability, runtime residuals, and memory checks passed; peak server memory was 6.70 GB. These local results did not establish successful board orchestration.

P2R0C1D23.title: Checking whether client/server rounding drift was depth-five specific
P2R0C1D23.summary: Run the unchanged, already-scored depth-four estimator through the official client/server path as a numerical control.
P2R0C1D23.result: It showed the same kind of tiny drift: RMS 2.67e-9 and maximum 1.1921e-7. The drift was therefore not unique to depth five and did not explain its board failures.

P2R0C1D27.title: Separating shared memory arenas to test aliasing overhead
P2R0C1D27.summary: Compare shared and split arena layouts while holding the 58-call computation and output bytes exactly fixed.
P2R0C1D27.result: Splitting saved only 0.683 ms median overhead, short of the 15 ms target, and used 2.32 GB more memory. With only about 222 MB left below the limit, the split layout was rejected.

P2R0G18A.title: Can 22 native features predict the missing late-layer state?
P2R0G18A.summary: Fit the fixed predictor from the estimator’s 22 native features and test its local q estimates and final predictions in four held-out folds.
P2R0G18A.result: Final MSE improved by 1.97% to 2.9889e-8, but closed only 2.46% of the gap to exact q. Both local and final-error requirements failed. This feature set was stopped; other q information sources were not ruled out.

P2R0G18B5A.title: No approval record was issued after the failed cross-validation
P2R0G18B5A.summary: Check that downstream approval and review artifacts were created only after a passing out-of-fold result.
P2R0G18B5A.result: The experiment failed, and neither approval artifact was issued. This closes the approval branch for that failed model; it is not a further estimator result.

P2R0G18B5E.title: Inference and export remained unexecuted after the model failed
P2R0G18B5E.summary: Prepare deployment inference and export machinery for the model, conditional on its empirical accuracy result.
P2R0G18B5E.result: The implementation received static review only. Model execution, export, parity, resource measurement, packaging, and submission remained unperformed after the empirical branch failed.

P2R0G18B5A2.title: Matching the output-review schema to the frozen experiment
P2R0G18B5A2.summary: Repair the post-run review tool so it accepts the experiment’s exact observation fields and rejects malformed, renamed, missing, or extra values.
P2R0G18B5A2.result: Independent review accepted the static implementation and field compatibility. No live output review, model refit, package, or submission was authorized or performed by this check.

P2R0G18B5C5.title: Static packaging review found two implementation defects
P2R0G18B5C5.summary: Review the frozen builder and runtime contract, including Python import order and whether retained package files still match their expected identities.
P2R0G18B5C5.result: Despite 389 static cases, review found unenforced future-import ordering and incomplete filename-to-inode revalidation. The frozen version was held and never cleared for live use; repairs required a new version.

P2R0G18D.title: Estimating the value of retuning the H selection parameter
P2R0G18D.summary: Bound the potential final-error improvement from choosing the exact minimum H before spending a one-shot nested selection experiment.
P2R0G18D.result: The estimated planning gain was 8.33e-12, only 0.9984% of the score deficit. Alternative-H outer effects were unmeasured. The idea remained a diagnostic, with insufficient value to justify the experiment.

P2R0G19A.title: Locating the source of late-layer mean error
P2R0G19A.summary: Use offline Monte Carlo truth to separate error in the propagated state from error in the formula that turns that state into layer means.
P2R0G19A.result: On both tested networks, the propagated state accounted for the error. With true state, the order-two formula’s error fell below sampling noise. Adding a fifth-cumulant formula was therefore the wrong repair for this deficit.

P2R0G19B_RESID.title: Small per-layer deficits accumulate into deep-state error
P2R0G19B_RESID.summary: Use a projected-truth probe to identify the roughly 1% missing contribution at each propagation step after the collective correction.
P2R0G19B_RESID.result: About 6.4% deep-plane error remained. The recorded decomposition attributed it to accumulating per-step deficits below the previous probe’s resolution. The next missing generator component was still unresolved.

P2R0G19B_CARRIER_MAPGAP.title: Does the gain come from a better formula or more retained state?
P2R0G19B_CARRIER_MAPGAP.summary: Separate the value of richer Mehler formulas from the value of carrying distinct tensor information between layers.
P2R0G19B_CARRIER_MAPGAP.result: Initial probes suggested both contribute, but the cost and achievable accuracy of a plane-only replacement remained unresolved. A candidate needed 8–10% adjusted improvement on the eight-network panel.

P2R0G19B_MATH_H4_REVERSE_RANK.title: Structural questions for reversing fourth-order corrections
P2R0G19B_MATH_H4_REVERSE_RANK.summary: Organize separate mathematical questions about a fourth-order reverse module and its quotient representation.
P2R0G19B_MATH_H4_REVERSE_RANK.result: This is an organizing record, not an independent proof or estimator result. Its structural claims have separate child records and must be resolved individually.

P2R0G19B_MATH_H6_TAIL.title: Bounding omitted sixth- and eighth-order terms
P2R0G19B_MATH_H6_TAIL.summary: Organize the separate tests needed to control the centered sixth- and eighth-order residual terms.
P2R0G19B_MATH_H6_TAIL.result: This is an organizing record. It reports no combined bound or numerical result; each structural child retains its own evidence and unresolved conditions.

P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_CONDITIONING.title: Can the available context determine the needed K31 action?
P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_CONDITIONING.summary: Test whether the proposed context measurements remain well-conditioned for the part of K31 that matters to final prediction, within the remaining compute budget.
P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_CONDITIONING.result: Unresolved. The construction needs a restricted singular-value bound and mismatch below 0.1811, or a counterexample that changes the target while remaining invisible to the context.

P2R0G19B_K31_DIRECT_ACTION_ZERO_HIDDEN_V.title: Exact K31 action and Bellman test remove channel-variance state
P2R0G19B_K31_DIRECT_ACTION_ZERO_HIDDEN_V.summary: Determine whether computing the exact scalar K31 contribution removes the need to carry uncertainty for that channel across layers.
P2R0G19B_K31_DIRECT_ACTION_ZERO_HIDDEN_V.result: With both the exact scalar action and full Bellman test retained, the channel is deterministic and needs no eighth-order or cross-layer covariance state. Uncertainty in proxy actions remains separate.

P2R0G19B_K31_DENSE_CAVITY_GUARANTEE.title: Dense weights do not guarantee cavity independence
P2R0G19B_K31_DENSE_CAVITY_GUARANTEE.summary: Check the premise that dense network weights alone make cavity variables independent or their spectra sufficiently spread out.
P2R0G19B_K31_DENSE_CAVITY_GUARANTEE.result: The generic premise was disproved. Independence requires a shared core kernel, which is generically zero. Any use of the approximation needs an explicit leakage certificate for the particular frozen network.

P2R0G19B_K31_TEMPORAL_HANKEL_RANK.title: Accumulating K31 contributions with one scalar
P2R0G19B_K31_TEMPORAL_HANKEL_RANK.summary: Determine the temporal state needed to combine local K31 actions into their final-output contribution.
P2R0G19B_K31_TEMPORAL_HANKEL_RANK.result: Once the local actions are available, one scalar Bellman accumulator is sufficient. This resolves temporal accumulation only; obtaining each local action remains a separate problem.

P2R0G19B_K31_NORMAL_ORDER_OWNERSHIP.title: Counting every K31 collision contribution exactly once
P2R0G19B_K31_NORMAL_ORDER_OWNERSHIP.summary: Reconcile the latent index patterns, external equality classes, and graph collisions in the scalar cumulant calculation.
P2R0G19B_K31_NORMAL_ORDER_OWNERSHIP.result: The algebraic accounting was resolved: the complete cumulant contains every contribution once. Alternative Möbius and q decompositions do not provide additional independent terms.

P2R0G19B_K31_TRUE_DEFECT_INTERFACE.title: Computing the part of K31 missing from the assembled state
P2R0G19B_K31_TRUE_DEFECT_INTERFACE.summary: Obtain the scalar contraction of the output weight with true K31 minus the K31 already assembled by the estimator.
P2R0G19B_K31_TRUE_DEFECT_INTERFACE.result: The current summaries do not expose the required true fourth-action term. A projected derivative or certified tensor-free factorization is still needed within roughly one matrix-multiplication equivalent.

P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_Z22_TRANSIENT.title: Using a transient K22 residual to correct the next K31 action
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_Z22_TRANSIENT.summary: Use the transient connected K22 component absent from CP4 squares and the pairing plane to supply a K31 action after dense mixing.
