P2R0H8.result: Submission #328586 completed all 100 networks with raw final-layer MSE 2.9409e-8 and adjusted score 2.1258e-8. The graded source and archive were preserved.

P2R0G1B.title: Stack Kerdock integration corrections across layers
P2R0G1B.summary: Price a multilayer structured-point correction that preserves the complete action at each layer.
P2R0G1B.result: Stopped before sampling. Even an optimistic relaxed construction required 255.657 billion query FLOPs, 39.012 billion above the available budget before construction and bias control.

P2R0G6.title: Locate the missing error state in late layers
P2R0G6.summary: Supply exact local error corrections at layers 10–15 to identify how much the estimator could improve with the right information.
P2R0G6.result: On 40 validation networks, MSE fell from 3.1072e-8 to 6.3151e-9. No single local defect sufficed. Direct Kerdock measurement was too noisy to supply these corrections; this is localization, not deployment.

P2R0G9.title: Continue training without increasing inference cost
P2R0G9.summary: Continue the unchanged residual model with fresh AdamW training, selecting a checkpoint using a separate stopping set.
P2R0G9.result: The protected 40-network MSE improved 0.3821%, from 3.1072e-8 to 3.0954e-8. Inference stayed unchanged, so the checkpoint adds no deployment FLOPs; it is a small reusable improvement.

P2R0G16.title: Add degree-8 and degree-10 Gaussian path terms
P2R0G16.summary: Verify and evaluate factorized higher-order path corrections, alone and combined with the degree-6 correction.
P2R0G16.result: No tested arm improved the compute-adjusted objective. The combined stack reached raw MSE 2.8540e-8 but projected adjusted score 1.2438e-8. Unfactorized triangle terms cost at least 13.194 trillion extra FLOPs.

P2R0G11D.title: Refit the local error head across all development networks
P2R0G11D.summary: Refit the frozen 22→64→64 network and test its correction across four folds and a protected validation set.
P2R0G11D.result: Out-of-fold MSE improved 1.636% over the previous head to 3.0662e-8, with all folds improving. It still lost to the native model’s 2.9737e-8, so it was a successful head repair without an absolute estimator win.

P2R0C1D14B.title: Use four-level Winograd products for cubic moments
P2R0C1D14B.summary: Deepen the cubic carrier’s Winograd matrix multiplication from three to four recursive levels, using preallocated scratch memory. The full estimator passes its measured resource and output-drift checks.
P2R0C1D14B.result: All three local calls passed resource, repeatability, and drift checks. Submission #328622 achieved raw MSE 2.9409e-8 and adjusted score 1.7836e-8, becoming the retained scored version.

P2R0C1D16.title: Pack five-layer tensor storage by allocation lifetime
P2R0C1D16.summary: Verify the unchanged estimator with lifetime-packed depth-5 storage in the official local and client/server runtimes.
P2R0C1D16.result: Repeatability, finite outputs, exact FLOP counts, and memory checks passed on the established fixtures. This validates those runtime paths, but does not explain board failures or certify unseen cases.

P2R0G12C8V2.title: Initialize the learned state from a nonlinear model
P2R0G12C8V2.summary: Reconstruct training folds without leakage and test a learned state initialized from the nonlinear-Z model.
P2R0G12C8V2.result: Out-of-fold MSE improved 0.324% over nonlinear-Z to 3.0440e-8, with all folds improving. It still lost to the native model and the retained compute-adjusted submission, so it was not deployed.

P2R0C1D24B.title: Explain the depth-5 package’s board-only failures
P2R0C1D24B.summary: Separate estimator behavior from archive ingestion, evaluator orchestration, and hidden-case failures.
P2R0C1D24B.result: Blocked: both archives failed generically on the board, while unchanged code passed official local and client/server checks. An organizer error report or faithful failing-case reproduction is needed.

P2R0C1D29-K42K51-S0.title: Propagate sixth-order terms from K42 and K51 pairs
P2R0C1D29-K42K51-S0.summary: Run the frozen pair-inheritance source and action calculation once, checking arithmetic, isolation, and resource cost.
P2R0C1D29-K42K51-S0.result: 33 of 34 checks passed, including the predicted 151.825 billion extra FLOPs. Instrumented residual time was 0.51095 s, above 0.4 s. The run stopped without opening targets or measuring estimator accuracy.

P2R0G18B1.title: Validate the data-manifest filter before row generation
P2R0G18B1.summary: Run the reviewed runtime controls for a signed-pair experiment before generating any data.
P2R0G18B1.result: An overbroad field-name filter rejected a permitted zero-valued audit counter. The one-use run stopped before data generation. This closes that runtime version, not the signed-pair mathematics.

P2R0G18B5B.title: Certify the pooled parameter for the signed-pair fit
P2R0G18B5B.summary: Check whether the failed signed-pair branch produced an authoritative pooled-H parameter record.
P2R0G18B5B.result: It did not. H=[16,16,16,16] was replayed only as a diagnostic. The failed branch cannot supply a certified pooled parameter without a new preregistered experiment.

P2R0G18B5F.title: Package the signed-pair correction only after validation
P2R0G18B5F.summary: Determine whether the signed-pair model has the evidence needed for export and official evaluation.
P2R0G18B5F.result: Its out-of-fold test failed. Static control checks do not establish model accuracy or permit packaging and submission; this branch was closed.

P2R0G18B5C2.title: Audit the frozen model-builder controls
P2R0G18B5C2.summary: Review the frozen 17-component build contract and its 399 adversarial cases, including ordering, provenance, and publication controls.
P2R0G18B5C2.result: Independent review found no material defects in the static controls. This certifies the build contract only; runtime execution, fitting, model export, and submission still require separate checks.

P2R0G18B5E2.title: Account for every verifier replay during model construction
P2R0G18B5E2.summary: Audit whether the deployment package accurately reports how often construction verification was replayed.
P2R0G18B5E2.result: The record claimed one verifier replay without limiting that count to final verification, although construction used more. Static parity and meter controls did not cure this accounting defect; no live export or measurement was authorized.

P2R0G18F.title: Choose signed-pair corrections by network characteristics
P2R0G18F.summary: Bound the benefit of enabling or disabling the correction separately for each network before designing a target-free selector.
P2R0G18F.result: Even a selector allowed to see targets gained only 7.6546e-12, about 0.9174% of the score deficit. That ceiling was too small; a post-hoc selector would also leak validation information.

P2R0G19B_CHAIN.title: Combine variance and higher-moment corrections
P2R0G19B_CHAIN.summary: Inject corrections to K21, K22, K31, and unit variances, and fit shared strengths using held-out networks.
P2R0G19B_CHAIN.result: Five-network leave-one-out testing gave a mean raw-error improvement of 15.8% ± 4.1%, positive in every fold. Exact inputs showed sub-1e-8 capacity; deployment still needs sufficiently accurate, affordable inputs.

P2R0G19B_FIRE.title: Require corrections to repay their compute cost
P2R0G19B_FIRE.summary: Compare the correction’s accuracy gain with its additional FLOPs, then verify integration in the submitted estimator.
P2R0G19B_FIRE.result: Blocked on an affordable input source and full integration. The proposed expensive source needed about 27% raw-error reduction just to break even; final acceptance requires at least 3% held-out adjusted gain.

P2R0G19B_MATH_NCQC_IDENTIFIABILITY.title: Observe trajectory-dependent quantities in NCQC
P2R0G19B_MATH_NCQC_IDENTIFIABILITY.summary: Collect the separate mathematical questions about which trajectory-dependent quantities the proposed representation can recover.
P2R0G19B_MATH_NCQC_IDENTIFIABILITY.result: Open. Each structural claim must be resolved independently; evidence for one child does not establish the others or a complete estimator.

P2R0G19B_MATH_COMMUTATOR_RANK.title: Bound commutator-algebra capacity and compute cost
P2R0G19B_MATH_COMMUTATOR_RANK.summary: Collect the separate claims needed to determine whether a commutator-based representation has sufficient capacity at feasible cost.
P2R0G19B_MATH_COMMUTATOR_RANK.result: Open. The component claims remain independently testable; this grouping itself establishes no capacity result or cost bound.

P2R0G19B_MATH_2PI_NCQC.title: Account for shared-core 2PI and q4 Gram calculations
P2R0G19B_MATH_2PI_NCQC.summary: Collect the separate mathematical and accounting claims for the shared-core representation and q4 Gram calculations.
P2R0G19B_MATH_2PI_NCQC.result: Open. The underlying structural questions must be resolved separately; no combined result is established by this grouping.

P2R0G19B_K31_RAW_GAIN_CERT.title: Certify a genuinely new scalar K31 correction
P2R0G19B_K31_RAW_GAIN_CERT.summary: Measure only the K31 contribution missing from the existing estimator; its already-included same-site scalar cannot add information.
P2R0G19B_K31_RAW_GAIN_CERT.result: Open: produce the residual within one remaining matrix-product equivalent, prove incremental gain above 2.86e-10, and keep total endpoint error at or below 3.80e-6.

P2R0G19B_K31_GENERIC_RECURRENT_CARRIER.title: Cost of carrying eleven fourth-order directions through depth
P2R0G19B_K31_GENERIC_RECURRENT_CARRIER.summary: Materialize and propagate the generic eleven-direction fourth-order representation across ten layers.
P2R0G19B_K31_GENERIC_RECURRENT_CARRIER.result: The explicit recurrent carrier costs about 110 matrix-product equivalents, beyond the 49-equivalent budget. Only approaches that contract the tensor before materializing it remain possible.

P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_INJECTIVITY.title: When rotated contexts identify a fixed tangent direction
P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_INJECTIVITY.summary: Prove that generic rotated observations distinguish a fixed finite-dimensional value tangent when the incidence codimension is large enough.
P2R0G19B_K31_CONTEXT_INJECTIVITY.result: A nonzero minor establishes pointwise injectivity. The theorem does not provide a uniform lower bound on conditioning, so injectivity alone does not ensure stable recovery.

P2R0G19B_K31_SCALAR_BELLMAN_TRANSPORT.title: Transport the leading K31 effect as one scalar per layer
P2R0G19B_K31_SCALAR_BELLMAN_TRANSPORT.summary: Factor the final-output derivative through local K31 maps so the leading correction can be accumulated without carrying a fourth-order Hermite tensor.
P2R0G19B_K31_SCALAR_BELLMAN_TRANSPORT.result: The scalar transport identity holds through order 1/n when the derivative-factorization assumption holds. It is a perturbative theorem, not a complete estimator implementation.

P2R0G19B_K31_BIPARTITE_ORIENTATION_NOGO.title: Moment invariants cannot determine matrix orientation
P2R0G19B_K31_BIPARTITE_ORIENTATION_NOGO.summary: Ask whether second- and third-order invariant information can select the physical matrix orientation within the larger factorization freedom.
P2R0G19B_K31_BIPARTITE_ORIENTATION_NOGO.result: It cannot. The moment-only bipartite construction is not deployable without a white-box anchor that fixes the required orientation.

P2R0G19B_K31_POST_AQ_H3_CARRIER.title: Carry an independent signed third-order residual
P2R0G19B_K31_POST_AQ_H3_CARRIER.summary: Use an independent H3 residual to supply both a signed third-order correction and a K31 defect through exact contractions.
P2R0G19B_K31_POST_AQ_H3_CARRIER.result: Open: a low-rank dictionary and reset rule must fit 49 matrix-product equivalents and deliver quartic gain of at least 2.86e-10. Tail rank or a nullspace obstruction could rule it out.

P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_211_PRIMITIVE.title: Recover hidden fourth-order directions that matter after reset
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_211_PRIMITIVE.summary: Study all-distinct and 211 tensor directions that the current repeated-moment interface cannot see but a later dense reset can expose.
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_211_PRIMITIVE.result: Open: find a target-free realizable source invisible to the old interface, then contract its full future effect within budget. Ambient tensor examples alone do not establish an available correction.

P2R0G19B_FORWARD_H4_FREIMAN_NOGO.title: Rank bound rules out a uniform fourth-order Hermite carrier
P2R0G19B_FORWARD_H4_FREIMAN_NOGO.summary: Bound the representation size needed to carry fourth-order information for 1024 independent quadratic cores.
P2R0G19B_FORWARD_H4_FREIMAN_NOGO.result: Polarization gives rank at least 45,090. One dense fourth-order transport plus the core already exceeds 49 matrix-product equivalents, closing this uniform autonomous construction.

P2R0G19B_Q211_COMMON_FACTOR_RECEIPT.title: Conditions for reusing one tensor factor at no extra product cost
P2R0G19B_Q211_COMMON_FACTOR_RECEIPT.summary: Check whether every new residual slice shares the stored factor and preserves its direction through all reverse resets.
P2R0G19B_Q211_COMMON_FACTOR_RECEIPT.result: Open: prove rank-one residual slices and factor collinearity at every active cut. Otherwise the calculation must pay the full higher-rank cost.

P2R0G19B_GRADED_ANTICOMMUTING_CARRIER.title: Use anticommuting structure to compress the q211 carrier
P2R0G19B_GRADED_ANTICOMMUTING_CARRIER.summary: Introduce an involution and odd cores that make the leading paid product skew-symmetric, then test whether later terms preserve the small representation.
P2R0G19B_GRADED_ANTICOMMUTING_CARRIER.result: Open: establish the source of the involution, preserved grading, closure of even words, and a final-output tail bound within budget. Higher-order returns may enlarge the representation.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_RANK50_TARGET_TAIL.title: Can a rank-50 model ignore the missing third-order directions?
P2R0G19B_NCQC_RANK50_TARGET_TAIL.summary: Test whether a rank-50 representation can be adequate despite lacking generic capacity for covariance and third moments together.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_RANK50_TARGET_TAIL.result: Open: the omitted third-order component must have sufficiently little endpoint value, with θ_K × λ_50 ≤ 0.0328064 and verified conditioning. Assuming isotropy is insufficient.

P2R0G19B_MINIMUM_STACK_A_B_C_OR_D.title: Three correction channels required by the capacity analysis
P2R0G19B_MINIMUM_STACK_A_B_C_OR_D.summary: Determine which variance, signed third-order, and fourth-order corrections are all necessary to cover the missing information.
P2R0G19B_MINIMUM_STACK_A_B_C_OR_D.result: The requirement is established: variance scale, a correctly separated signed H3 contribution, and strict quartic completion. Z22 can replace the last only with full interface and error coverage. No implementation is certified.

P2R0G19B_Z22_GENERIC_COST_NOGO.title: Cost of acquiring the complete Z22 action
P2R0G19B_Z22_GENERIC_COST_NOGO.summary: Price the generic K31 and crossed-K22 masks after removing all information already represented by the estimator.
P2R0G19B_Z22_GENERIC_COST_NOGO.result: Their effective ranks are at least 947 and 980, requiring about ten products across the suffix. This rules out the generic additive route with only one product-equivalent available.

P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_CONDITIONING.title: Stabilize the two-ray signed CP representation
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_CONDITIONING.summary: Choose the singleton sign so the denominator becomes 1+|ρ| instead of 1−ρ.
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_CONDITIONING.result: The resulting amplification is at most one; |ρ|=1 collapses to information already present in pairwise terms. This algebraic result requires the deployed representation to permit the sign flip.

P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_OWNERSHIP.title: Conditions for a small Clifford-supported representation
P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_OWNERSHIP.summary: Test whether a balanced rank-54 support can keep the spin-factor representation small throughout later propagation.
P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_OWNERSHIP.result: Open: verify the common support and account for kernel directions, radial terms, and future returns into new information. Those terms must be represented already or proven unreachable.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_FULL_AQ_R49_REPLACEMENT.title: Replace the existing stage with a rank-49 full-AQ model
P2R0G19B_NCQC_FULL_AQ_R49_REPLACEMENT.summary: Include both linear and quadratic coefficients to seek a smaller joint covariance and third-moment representation.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_FULL_AQ_R49_REPLACEMENT.result: The dimension and cost calculation is promising only as a replacement of the existing D14 stage. Initialization, stable recovery, equivalent value, and a supplied higher-order residual remain unproved.

P2R0G19B_AQ_CARRIED_PROJECTION_Q211.title: A quadratic projection does not contain every fourth cumulant
P2R0G19B_AQ_CARRIED_PROJECTION_Q211.summary: Compare the fourth cumulant of the carried degree-at-most-two projection with that of the full AQ variable.
P2R0G19B_AQ_CARRIED_PROJECTION_Q211.result: The carried state contains only its own fourth cumulant. The discarded difference can be nonzero even for an affine Gaussian ReLU; covariance information alone does not supply that connected fourth-order term.

P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_SIGNED_SURFACE_SOUR.title: One signed fourth-order scalar for a fixed final output
P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_SIGNED_SURFACE_SOUR.summary: After accounting for existing terms and repeated indices, contract the dependent joint cumulant-generating function directly against one fixed endpoint.
P2R0G19B_Q211_DIRECT_SIGNED_SURFACE_SOUR.result: One contracted fourth derivative is sufficient in information terms. A usable method still must obtain it from the actual distribution and price the full positive-depth query; pairwise Gaussian information is insufficient.

P2R0G19B_FULL_AQ_AFFINE_SEAM_SCHUR_THRES.title: Rank needed to recover missing covariance directions
P2R0G19B_FULL_AQ_AFFINE_SEAM_SCHUR_THRES.summary: Analyze the exact Schur map through which a quadratic prefix can recover covariance directions absent at an affine boundary.
P2R0G19B_FULL_AQ_AFFINE_SEAM_SCHUR_THRES.result: At zero quadratic coefficient, the missing dimension is (n−r)(n−r+1)/2. The rank theorem covers r49, r54, and r55; actual recovery still requires separate rank and conditioning certificates.

P2R0G19B_AQ_L4_SECTION_ACQUISITION_COST.title: Include factor recovery in the AQ runtime budget
P2R0G19B_AQ_L4_SECTION_ACQUISITION_COST.summary: Price the step from moment and response matrices to an oriented AQ factor representation.
P2R0G19B_AQ_L4_SECTION_ACQUISITION_COST.result: Open: existing sub-49-product totals omit the covariance square root, orientation solve, gauge choice, and stability across networks. A reusable factor map must be shown explicitly or these costs must be added.

P2R0G19B_AQ_R44_EXACT_FRAME_CANDIDATE.title: Rank-44 AQ representation across ten layers
P2R0G19B_AQ_R44_EXACT_FRAME_CANDIDATE.summary: Carry all nine required interior Gram matrices using about 48.59 matrix-product equivalents.
P2R0G19B_AQ_R44_EXACT_FRAME_CANDIDATE.result: Its idealized capacity diagnostic is the first such rank below raw 1e-8. Actual recovery, reset errors, and coherent omitted terms remain unproved and must fit a narrow 0.01239 normalized error allowance.

P2R0G19B_Q211_RELU_SCHUR_GENERIC_FULL_RA.title: A ReLU reset generically expands q211 to full width
P2R0G19B_Q211_RELU_SCHUR_GENERIC_FULL_RA.summary: Test whether a small local tensor support survives multiplication by the ReLU gate-overlap matrix.
P2R0G19B_Q211_RELU_SCHUR_GENERIC_FULL_RA.result: With a full-rank gate Gram and a full-support factor, one reset expands the support to width N. Generic support limits of five or seventeen fail unless existing information and endpoint-only effects are factored out.

P2R0G19B_Q211_SIGNED_MATRIX_COST_VALUE.title: Trade signed-matrix rank against correction cost
P2R0G19B_Q211_SIGNED_MATRIX_COST_VALUE.summary: Represent accumulated q211 births with a signed matrix and price its rank across ten layers.
P2R0G19B_Q211_SIGNED_MATRIX_COST_VALUE.result: Before source acquisition, cost is about 0.21484q+0.32227 products for rank q. One extra product permits only about rank three. Useful residual rank, repeated-index accounting, memory, and accuracy remain open.

P2R0G19B_AQ55_D14_RESIDENT_VIEW_ESCAPE.title: Reuse existing AQ factors at the late-layer boundary
P2R0G19B_AQ55_D14_RESIDENT_VIEW_ESCAPE.summary: Search the existing D14 buffers and shared calculations for already-oriented rank-55 AQ factors and the required endpoint information.
P2R0G19B_AQ55_D14_RESIDENT_VIEW_ESCAPE.result: Open: identify actual arrays, operation identities, lifetimes, orientation, and repeated-index accounting. Without this reuse, a new forward or reverse representation does not fit the proposed architecture.

P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_VALUE_GATE.title: Prove that a cheap Price trace adds new accuracy
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_VALUE_GATE.summary: Remove Gaussian pairings, repeated indices, and all previously represented information before valuing the trace correction.
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_VALUE_GATE.result: Open: demonstrate incremental gain of at least 2.86e-10 after query and arithmetic errors. A cheap contraction alone does not establish useful new endpoint information.

P2R0G19B_AQ_CONNECTED_CUMULANT_EXPONENT_.title: The infinite AQ cumulant response need not converge
P2R0G19B_AQ_CONNECTED_CUMULANT_EXPONENT_.summary: Test whether small higher cumulants justify an analytic infinite-cumulant expansion of the ReLU response.
P2R0G19B_AQ_CONNECTED_CUMULANT_EXPONENT_.result: A normalized chi-square example has response terms that eventually grow for every nonzero deformation. The proposed analytic series has zero radius; a finite or exact identity is needed instead.

P2R0G19B_AQ_L5_R62_R63_SECTION_FRONTIER.title: Compare rank 62 and rank 63 across five resets
P2R0G19B_AQ_L5_R62_R63_SECTION_FRONTIER.summary: Compare the arithmetic and conditioning of the two candidate factor representations.
P2R0G19B_AQ_L5_R62_R63_SECTION_FRONTIER.result: Rank 62 costs 47.43295 products; rank 63 costs 48.07040. The extra 0.63745 removes a universal 561-mode first-order nullspace and improves difficult-mode conditioning. Neither yet has a validated usable factor map.

P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_COVARIANCE_ANCH.title: Anchor AQ covariance using the live CP4 square frame
P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_COVARIANCE_ANCH.summary: Use the normalized CP4 frame to choose a factor orientation and construct the remaining covariance from its square root.
P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_COVARIANCE_ANCH.result: The construction reproduces covariance exactly and respects neuron and factor transformations. It does not yet establish K21 recovery, full-boundary rank, numerical roots, runtime, or convergence.

P2R0G19B_R62_SECOND_DIFFERENCE_ANCHOR_NO.title: Disjoint second differences lose 33 anchor directions
P2R0G19B_R62_SECOND_DIFFERENCE_ANCHOR_NO.summary: Test a proposed rank-62 construction built from disjoint affine second-difference triples.
P2R0G19B_R62_SECOND_DIFFERENCE_ANCHOR_NO.result: An explicit annihilating direction limits the proposed 561-dimensional block to rank at most 528. The construction fails regardless of background correction; a different stencil structure is required.

P2R0G19B_H3_D11_DISTINGUISHED_SLOT_NOGO.title: Existing symmetric CP3 data cannot cheaply recover slot orientation
P2R0G19B_H3_D11_DISTINGUISHED_SLOT_NOGO.summary: Ask whether the current stored third-order information exposes a pair-versus-singleton direction needed by the new correction.
P2R0G19B_H3_D11_DISTINGUISHED_SLOT_NOGO.result: It does not. Generic recovery has rank proportional to width and exceeds the rank-62/63 runtime margins. Reopening requires an explicitly available low-rank slot interface with new endpoint value.

P2R0G19B_PRICE_AQ55_LIVENESS_COST_HOLD.title: A stored AQ Gram does not supply the required Price trace
P2R0G19B_PRICE_AQ55_LIVENESS_COST_HOLD.summary: Check whether the paid AQ calculations also retain the pushed Star31 quantity needed by the trace correction.
P2R0G19B_PRICE_AQ55_LIVENESS_COST_HOLD.result: They retain the Gram but not the full Star31 object. Reconstructing it across six boundaries exceeds the remaining 0.803 product-equivalents; direct reuse or a certified low-rank contraction is required.

P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_CONSTANT_PRICE_REFIT_V.title: Fit ten K22 features from one constant Price mode
P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_CONSTANT_PRICE_REFIT_V.summary: Propagate one target-free constant mode, form its q211 contribution to K22, and remove existing estimator responses jointly from the ten new layer scalars.
P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_CONSTANT_PRICE_REFIT_V.result: Open: the unfused baseline costs about 30 float32 products. A cheaper rank-one identity still needs repeated-index and overlap checks. The fitted feature must exceed 0.8124 held-out correlation.

P2R0G19B_AQ_SQUARE_GAUSSIAN_OWNERSHIP_FR.title: Separate new connected energy from Gaussian square energy
P2R0G19B_AQ_SQUARE_GAUSSIAN_OWNERSHIP_FR.summary: Decompose a quadratic core’s squared contribution into Gaussian pairings and genuinely connected fourth-order information.
P2R0G19B_AQ_SQUARE_GAUSSIAN_OWNERSHIP_FR.result: The connected fraction is 2/(r_eff+2); total excess over the matched Gaussian square is 6/(r_eff+6). The earlier 0.983 whole-square fidelity mostly measured Gaussian energy already present.

P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_PSD_SCALE_GA.title: Limit polynomial-feature amplitude to preserve covariance
P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_PSD_SCALE_GA.summary: Scale the proposed Gram matrix so the residual covariance remains positive semidefinite.
P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_PSD_SCALE_GA.result: The maximum squared amplitude is the reciprocal of the largest whitened Gram eigenvalue. Connected signal then scales as the fourth power of amplitude, so feasibility by shrinking may erase the accuracy gain.

P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_TARGET_VALUE.title: Measure the actual value of a polynomial Gram correction
P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_TARGET_VALUE.summary: Test the joint fitted or fixed-map effect after accounting for cross-layer correlation and alignment with the true error.
P2R0G19B_AQ_POLYNOMIAL_GRAM_TARGET_VALUE.result: Open: local positivity gives no positive lower bound on raw-error gain. The joint test must exceed 1.9409e-8 gain after all boundary and remainder errors.

P2R0G19B_FIVE_RESET_CAUSAL_CHI_THEOREM.title: Track correlated errors across five resets
P2R0G19B_FIVE_RESET_CAUSAL_CHI_THEOREM.summary: Determine the cross-correlation information needed to combine reset errors exactly rather than treating them as independent noise.
P2R0G19B_FIVE_RESET_CAUSAL_CHI_THEOREM.result: One causal cross scalar per reset suffices for sequential exactness. Final-only scoring needs one aggregate cross term and final norm. The six-block correlation geometry gives exact best and worst endpoint energies.

P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_GENERIC_BROAD_LEDGE.title: Full physical q211 acquisition exceeds the runtime budget
P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_GENERIC_BROAD_LEDGE.summary: Count the matrix products needed for the complete physical q211 action, including repeated-index corrections.
P2R0G19B_AFFINE_Q211_GENERIC_BROAD_LEDGE.result: Generic strict off-diagonal rank is at least 980, making one fully formed boundary action cost at least 987 product-equivalents. Only proven low-rank, single-feature, or fused-product alternatives remain.

P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_OLD_SUBTRACTI.title: Remove previously represented terms from a radial mixture
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_OLD_SUBTRACTI.summary: Subtract the Gaussian plane, linear variance/fourth-order response, and induced mean outer products from the full mixture covariance.
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_OLD_SUBTRACTI.result: The exact subtraction formula is established and prevents mean shifts from being counted as new covariance value. The remaining signal’s magnitude and fidelity still need to be measured.

P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_ACTION_DEFECT_GRAM.title: Measure one endpoint’s recoverable rank-63 action
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_ACTION_DEFECT_GRAM.summary: Project the endpoint-adjoint quantity λN₀ onto the subspace specified by the section theorem to determine its exact first-order gain factor.
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_ACTION_DEFECT_GRAM.result: The action is invisible exactly when that projection vanishes. Cancelling action a requires norm at least |a|/√γ. Actual endpoint data, γ, available radius, and higher-order error remain to be certified.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_K21_RIGHT_INVERSE_EQUIVARI.title: Recover K21 with a transformation-consistent pseudoinverse
P2R0G19B_AQ63_K21_RIGHT_INVERSE_EQUIVARI.summary: Use a projected-Veronese Moore–Penrose right inverse to recover K21 without arbitrary latent-coordinate ordering.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_K21_RIGHT_INVERSE_EQUIVARI.result: The inverse respects neuron permutations and the declared orthogonal factor transformations. This proves equivariance only; uniqueness, singular-value bounds, branch selection, and arithmetic remain separate checks.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_SPLIT_SIMPLE_NO.title: Rank-63 split-simple cubic-null spaces are too small
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_SPLIT_SIMPLE_NO.summary: Bound the dimension of cubic-null spaces containing a split-simple element with paired positive and negative eigenvalues.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_SPLIT_SIMPLE_NO.result: Their dimension is at most 1022, below the 1023 directions required for a strict K21 right inverse; with transverse anticommutant it is at most 992. Exceptional spaces without such an element remain unresolved.

P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_STREAMING_.title: Stream the extra degree-7 and degree-9 channels
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_STREAMING_.summary: Add the exact biased pair contributions without materializing all intermediate arrays at once.
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_STREAMING_.result: Open: the naive 18 extra channels need about 576 MiB of scratch and 144 MiB of weights, plus roughly 18/17 of the current kernel arithmetic. A streamed implementation must fit the remaining budget.

P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_RAW_VALUE_.title: Validate the incremental value of the completion feature
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_RAW_VALUE_.summary: Evaluate the K21/K31 feature after removing its overlap with everything the estimator already represents.
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_RAW_VALUE_.result: No held-out endpoint result is established. Reaching raw MSE below 1e-8 requires gain of at least 1.9409e-8 and residual correlation of at least 0.8124, with bias, positivity, and runtime also controlled.

P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_OLD_OVERLAP_GATE.title: Subtract existing responses from the sixth-order source
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_OLD_OVERLAP_GATE.summary: Identify which part of the proposed L6 action adds information beyond the Q24 and CP3/CP4 responses.
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_OLD_OVERLAP_GATE.result: Open: Q24 includes the r⁻¹ H4 source but not the declared L6 source. Other columns can still reproduce its endpoint action, so full response-space subtraction and same-order error bounds are required.

P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_OUTPUT_COLLISION_SUB.title: Remove repeated output indices in quadratic time
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_OUTPUT_COLLISION_SUB.summary: Compute the equal-output-index correction for a strict rank-one K22 endpoint after the main product.
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_OUTPUT_COLLISION_SUB.result: The correction is an explicit O(n²) reduction and needs no second dense product. This resolves output-index collisions only; overlap with lower-order source terms must still be handled separately.

P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_TAIL_BOUND.title: Bound the omitted terms in the leading q211 trace
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_TAIL_BOUND.summary: Bound the local tensor error after retaining the leading xy surface term for correlations of magnitude at most ρ.
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_TAIL_BOUND.result: The absolute remainder is at most ρ³/π²+5ρ⁴/(12π)+ε₅ before endpoint amplification. No uniform relative bound follows when the leading action is small or signed terms cancel.

P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_LEAF_ONE_PRODUCT_I.title: Contract a rank-one q211 plane with one dense product
P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_LEAF_ONE_PRODUCT_I.summary: For a source plane P=uuᵀ, reduce the K22 action to H=R Diag(u) Wᵀ plus quadratic-time reductions.
P2R0G19B_Q211_RANKONE_LEAF_ONE_PRODUCT_I.result: The action identity is exact after consistent repeated-index accounting. It applies to a rank-one source factor; it does not prove that the physical source plane itself has rank one.

P2R0G19B_R55_NORMAL_QUOTIENT_SPLIT.title: Split the rank-55 quotient into symmetric and stabilizer parts
P2R0G19B_R55_NORMAL_QUOTIENT_SPLIT.summary: Decompose the final quotient and use the Hessian appropriate to its nonorthogonal coordinate frame.
P2R0G19B_R55_NORMAL_QUOTIENT_SPLIT.result: The exact split has 524800 symmetric channels and 969 stabilizer channels. Separate ranks of these blocks do not establish the rank of their combined Schur map.

P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_LITERAL_COST.title: Price three mixed Hessian directions at one common boundary
P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_LITERAL_COST.summary: Compute BC+CB, AC+CA, and AB+BA using the same eigensystem and resolvent data.
P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_LITERAL_COST.result: Open: show the actual shared calculations and added rotation and quadrature work within budget. Products from a different reset or unrelated Jordan calculation do not establish reuse.

P2R0G19B_QHEAD_START5_ORACLE.title: Accuracy possible with exact local state from layer five
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_START5_ORACLE.summary: Supply the exact start-5 q-state to test whether this correction location has enough capacity.
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_START5_ORACLE.result: Held-fold raw MSE was 4.6985e-10. This demonstrates oracle capacity only: a deployable method still must recover enough of that state without access to targets.

P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RELEASE_SCOPE.title: Limit the four-field fit to one paired validation run
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RELEASE_SCOPE.summary: Check the exact permitted scope of the frozen four-field input experiment.
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_RELEASE_SCOPE.result: The frozen authorization covered one paired fold-0 observer fit. Static review established scope, not accuracy; retries, other folds, full refitting, integration, metering, packaging, and submission remained unauthorized.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RELEASE_REPAIR.title: Prepare an isolated four-network learned-state evaluation
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RELEASE_REPAIR.summary: Design the fresh-data experiment with separated simulation and fit records, independent sampling streams, and sequential checks on four preselected networks.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RELEASE_REPAIR.result: Paused with no data or result. The first implementation failed static review and its repair is also paused. Resumption requires a separate raw-MSE diagnostic below 1e-8 and review; full evaluation checks remain.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_DIRECT_AUDIT.title: Audit data isolation before learned-state evaluation
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_DIRECT_AUDIT.summary: Independently check selection order, delayed target access, simulation-state separation, response orientation, and stopping rules.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_V2R1_DIRECT_AUDIT.result: Paused with no result. The audit can resume only after the separate diagnostic is strictly below 1e-8 and the branch is reviewed; any failed invariant stops the experiment before labels are released.

P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.title: Static review of the single-network learned-state diagnostic
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.summary: Check the frozen provider, response formulas, zero-input control, MSE calculation, and numerical acceptance rules.
P2R0G19B_PHYSICAL_V34_RANK35_DESCRIPTIVE.result: The candidate-specific static review passed, but the handoff is paused and no diagnostic result exists. This review does not itself authorize target access or establish accuracy.

P2R0G19B_G3_INSTRUMENT_SUITE.title: Build reference measurements for variance-correction experiments
P2R0G19B_G3_INSTRUMENT_SUITE.summary: Store layerwise covariance residual targets for two networks and define a consistent metric for their propagated variance effect.
P2R0G19B_G3_INSTRUMENT_SUITE.result: The measurement suite is complete. Exact variance inputs reached raw MSE 1.25–1.46e-8. The K21 Frobenius metric was uninformative at 400000 samples; the propagated variance metric is used instead.

P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB3_SUPPLY_LADDER.title: Replace each moment input with truth to locate the bottleneck
P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB3_SUPPLY_LADDER.summary: Test exact fourth moments, third moments, and K21 inputs separately and together in the deployed correction engine.
P2R0G19B_PKG_SUB3_SUPPLY_LADDER.result: The current engine reduced error 10.6%; making these inputs exact gave only 7.5%. Exact pre-planes through the tangent gave 34.8%, while exact states gave 47.4%. These are oracle diagnostics, not deployable supplies.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2A_EMISSION.title: Compare the two formulas that generate the K21 plane
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2A_EMISSION.summary: Evaluate the dense engine and deployed estimator on the same carried state to isolate a possible emission-formula error.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_2A_EMISSION.result: They agreed to about 1e-5 RMS, roughly 50 times smaller than the truth gap and uncorrelated with it. The direct difference correction gave no gain; the emission formula was not the missing mechanism.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_3_COV.title: Replace propagated covariance with exact covariance
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_3_COV.summary: Test whether errors in off-diagonal covariance explain the missing variance correction.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_3_COV.result: An independent-truth diagnostic showed potential value, but the final in-estimator test added nothing on either network once mean, variance, third, and fourth moments were supplied. This tested route was closed.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_5_HIGHER_ORDER.title: Separate missing carried information from nonlinear response error
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_5_HIGHER_ORDER.summary: Use exact-input and response experiments to identify whether deeper propagation or the final conversion formula limits variance corrections.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N1_5_HIGHER_ORDER.result: The apparent large nonlinear-response gain was same-sample noise; going beyond linearization added at most 0.6 percentage points. Independent-truth tests instead identified third moments, tensor planes, and covariance as useful channels.

P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_FOURTH_PLANES.title: Restore the missing magnitude of K22 and K31 at depth
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_FOURTH_PLANES.summary: Measure fourth-order plane shrinkage and test exact or recursively generated replacements inside the estimator.
P2R0G19B_MECH_N0_1C_FOURTH_PLANES.result: Deep planes were 2–3 times too small. Exact planes improved the uncorrected host sharply, but 84% of the effect overlapped the learned correction. An affordable replacement with new held-out value remains open.

P2R0E3A3.title: Third-order Hermite residual versus CP3 state
P2R0E3A3.summary: Compare a third-order Hermite residual with the existing CP3 representation, after the preceding moment test passes.
P2R0E3A3.result: The comparison could not run: its required predecessor produced nonfinite or catastrophic results. Changing that prerequisite would be a different experiment.

P2R0H2.title: Locate rare late-layer instabilities
P2R0H2.summary: Inspect layer-by-layer errors using the organizer-provided observer_fit targets to find where rare failures begin.
P2R0H2.result: The diagnostic procedure is established within the permitted data role. It does not join network names to public scores or leaderboard results.

P2R0H3E.title: CS3B estimator and rejected test runners
P2R0H3E.summary: Freeze the corrected hybrid CS3B estimator and audit the software that would test it before running the candidate.
P2R0H3E.result: The estimator passed static source review; projected cost was 99.68% of budget. Both test runners were rejected for defects before execution. No measured cost or accuracy result exists.

P2R0H5.title: Submission #328277: final-layer error above target
P2R0H5.summary: Evaluate the near-floor-min estimator on the public board against the raw final-layer MSE target of 1e-8.
P2R0H5.result: Raw final-layer MSE was 8.75864e-8, about 5.14% better than #328273 but still above target. Adjusted score was 8.47513e-8; no all-layer result was supplied.

P2R0F2B.title: Ridge correction with richer features
P2R0F2B.summary: Learn a ridge correction from richer local features, then let it use its own predicted state through the network.
P2R0F2B.result: With supplied intermediate states, MSE reached 8.29e-9; autonomous MSE exploded to 0.346. This closes the tested ridge model, not the unexecuted structured variants.

P2R0F2H.title: State-independent Duhamel correction
P2R0F2H.summary: Test whether local input features alone can predict the correction needed during propagation, without learned state context.
P2R0F2H.result: Cross-validated final MSE was 3.90810e-8, 18.54% worse than the reference. The worst network also missed its limit. The tested state-independent correction was rejected.

P2R0F2N.title: Rank-16 covariance correction
P2R0F2N.summary: Represent correlations between prediction errors with a network-adaptive rank-16 covariance model.
P2R0F2N.result: MSE improved only 0.104% to 3.23012e-8 and failed all accuracy gates. Even truth-derived coefficients in the same rank-16 span reached only 2.89283e-8, still above target.

P2R0C1D1.title: Fixed-feature correction on a CP1536 model
P2R0C1D1.summary: Add a fixed 128-feature scalar correction to the CP1536 model and compare supplied-state and autonomous predictions.
P2R0C1D1.result: Both versions missed the 1e-7 target by more than 12.5×. Their MSEs differed by only 1.25%, pointing to limited local feature capacity rather than accumulated recurrence drift.

P2R0F2S.title: Where propagation error enters the model
P2R0F2S.summary: Measure how error appears and accumulates through layers, then identify the mathematical terms associated with it.
P2R0F2S.result: About 83% of final error came from propagated earlier errors. Fourth-order pair structure was the leading measured association. The analysis proposed extending the pair series; it did not modify the model.

P2R0F2X.title: λ³ Edgeworth shell correction
P2R0F2X.summary: Add the λ³ terms of the Edgeworth shell to the Q24 model, then refit the learned correction on its changed residuals.
P2R0F2X.result: The base model improved 9.97%, but the corrected system worsened 0.943% to 3.13655e-8. The shell removed errors the learned correction already handled; this combination was rejected.

P2R0F3A6.title: Fourth-cumulant loss during propagation
P2R0F3A6.summary: Substitute measured cumulants to distinguish errors in the stored state from errors in the formula that converts state to means.
P2R0F3A6.result: Across three networks, the fourth cumulant started accurate but lost about 7% per layer; by layer 15 it was 40–50% of truth. Supplied true cumulants improved the means, locating a state-propagation defect.

P2R0F3A8D.title: New internal features for a small learned correction
P2R0F3A8D.summary: Use features recorded from the revised model to predict the remaining per-unit errors.
P2R0F3A8D.result: Features identified harder networks but weakly predicted unit errors. The corrected 200-network cross-validation improved only 1.43% to 3.28726e-8. This feature set was closed.

P2R0F3A6B4.title: Carry the discarded K31 and fourth-cumulant residuals
P2R0F3A6B4.summary: Retain two residuals discarded at each reset and propagate them with independently verified exact formulas.
P2R0F3A6B4.result: The fourth-cumulant state became more accurate, but final mean error worsened 2.7% overall and lost on all three networks. The tested carry was rejected despite its improved state metric.

P2R0F3B2A.title: Direct fifth-order moment propagation
P2R0F3B2A.summary: Carry fifth-order diagonal and two-index quantities using exact propagation formulas, then test autonomous stability.
P2R0F3B2A.result: The formulas verified to numerical precision, but both small-network runs became severely unstable. One-step supplied-state gains did not survive recurrence. This rejects the implemented partial-state carry only.

P2R0F3B2B3.title: Structured fifth-order residual representation
P2R0F3B2B3.summary: Preserve exact repeated-index terms separately and compress only the fifth-order residual, paired with a covariance-resummed base.
P2R0F3B2B3.result: The earlier TT16 and whole-tensor CP8/16 forms are closed. This different residual representation remains conditional on a missing base-model theorem, then symmetry, accuracy and combined-cost proofs.

P2R0F3B2B2B.title: Finite independent-base cumulant algebra
P2R0F3B2B2B.summary: Construct permutation-equivariant algebra for third-, fourth- and fifth-order collision terms on an independent base.
P2R0F3B2B2B.result: The formal algebra is valid, with a 6,808-FLOP subtotal if its inputs already exist. Producing those inputs, correlated-case checks, numerical accuracy and deployment are outside this result.

P2R0F3C.title: Degree-8 Hermite control variate
P2R0F3C.summary: Use a degree-8 Hermite approximation to reduce late-layer sampling variance, provided its true expected values are available.
P2R0F3C.result: Gaussian variance capture was 99.89%, but no certified provider of the required layer-15 moments exists. Reusing samples cancels the benefit; an independent full-cost split is worse than plain Monte Carlo.

P2R0C1D7.title: Staged tensor contractions for CP3
P2R0C1D7.summary: Factor CP3 contractions into staged NumPy einsum operations to reduce their implementation cost.
P2R0C1D7.result: After an initial accounting failure, the revised tiny test passed. The integrated implementation still failed resource limits, closing this Python/NumPy form.

P2R0G1.title: Kerdock resets of internal network state
P2R0G1.summary: Use Kerdock-based internal-state information to reset accumulated prediction error within the existing model.
P2R0G1.result: Exact mean resets through layer 9 still gave MSE 3.1604e-8; complete directional state exceeded the available ray budget. These interfaces are closed. A cheaper nonlinear interface would require a new result.

P2R0G1B1.title: Exact mean resets through layers 7 and 9
P2R0G1B1.summary: Give the existing recurrence perfect mean residuals at several intermediate layers to test how much those resets could help.
P2R0G1B1.result: Resetting through layer 7 matched a single layer-7 reset. Extending through layer 9 reached 3.16039e-8, closing only 11.72% of the gap to supplied-state performance. More resets of this type were rejected.

P2R0G7.title: Reconstruct the Phase 1 Kerdock method for Phase 2
P2R0G7.summary: Rebuild the original Phase 1 sampling rule and low-layer moment resets, and separately replay the later empirical-gate control variate.
P2R0G7.result: All tested rank-0 forms failed the endpoint accuracy gate. The best snapped construction reached about 7.75e-8 and had wrong-signed correlation with truth. This sampled-state family was closed.

P2R0G10.title: Earlier training checkpoints for autonomous prediction
P2R0G10.summary: Test whether using an earlier checkpoint, with less exposure to supplied intermediate states, reduces autonomous rollout error.
P2R0G10.result: Every checkpoint from epochs 1–5 was worse than epoch 6, whose MSE was 3.10724e-8. Choosing an earlier checkpoint did not fix the missing-state problem.

P2R0G11A.title: Reverse-action K21 features
P2R0G11A.summary: Add rank-4, rank-8 and rank-16 reverse-action features from the Q24 state to predict local q errors using weights alone.
P2R0G11A.result: All three feature banks worsened the held-coordinate MSE from 5.49816e-9. The tested features were rejected before a multi-network run; a larger rank was not justified.

P2R0G11F.title: Full-688 correction integrated into D4
P2R0G11F.summary: Insert the correction fitted on all 688 networks into the D4 implementation and test the official resource limits.
P2R0G11F.result: Output and source checks passed, but one tested network took 0.42358 seconds against the 0.4-second residual limit. The run stopped; this implementation was not packaged.

P2R0C1D14C.title: Memory limit of the unpacked depth-5 implementation
P2R0C1D14C.summary: Estimate memory use when the depth-5 implementation keeps its original allocation schedule.
P2R0C1D14C.result: The unchanged design projected above 8.8 GB and was closed. A later lifetime-packed implementation measured below 7 GB, so this is not an impossibility result for depth 5.

P2R0C1D16A.title: Packed depth-5 FLOP accounting mismatch
P2R0C1D16A.summary: Check the packed depth-5 implementation against its declared FLOP count using local FlopScope 0.10.
P2R0C1D16A.result: The first call passed output, time and memory checks, but its bill exceeded the registered count by 125,829,120 FLOPs. The run stopped before the remaining calls; this accounting form was closed.

P2R0G12C8G.title: Global suffix context for the C8v2 correction
P2R0G12C8G.summary: Add information about the remaining layers to C8v2 while keeping cross-validation training and held-out networks separate.
P2R0G12C8G.result: All four folds improved, but the overall gain was only 0.103%, below the required 0.25%. Protected, native-model and compute-adjusted comparisons also failed, so this variant was rejected.

P2R0C1D25.title: Depth-5 propagation with depth-4 state reads
P2R0C1D25.summary: Combine the cheaper depth-5 propagation with depth-4 reads to reduce computation and memory.
P2R0C1D25.result: The hybrid saved 27.3 billion FLOPs and 651 MB, but one network took 0.41212 seconds, above the 0.4-second limit. The one-shot run stopped without packaging or submission.

P2R0G17.title: Non-Gaussian sixth-order terms spanning three or more units
P2R0G17.summary: Supply connected sixth-order information involving at least three distinct units, which is absent in the Gaussian model and too large to store densely.
P2R0G17.result: The only concrete provider, a difference-replica construction, failed all 315 screened cases. No executable alternative remains in this record; reopening requires a new design with viable sampling variance at budget.

P2R0G18B2.title: Runtime V4 diagnostic-history memory leak
P2R0G18B2.summary: Run the frozen experiment runtime while tracking its resource accounting and retained diagnostic data.
P2R0G18B2.result: The run was interrupted after diagnostic history grew nearly linearly. An independent audit traced this to FlopScope retaining completed rows. No result bundle was published; this runtime version was closed.

P2R0G18B5C.title: All-688 refit blocked by failed cross-validation
P2R0G18B5C.summary: Refit on all 688 networks only after the underlying experimental branch earns the right to proceed.
P2R0G18B5C.result: The runtime passed static review, but the branch failed cross-validation. No refit, model or execution authority followed; a different registered scientific proposal is required.

P2R0G18B5F0.title: Static review of the V1R3 submission controls
P2R0G18B5F0.summary: Audit the frozen software that would check provenance, validation records and one-use authority before a submission.
P2R0G18B5F0.result: Independent reviews accepted the static controls. No live package, empirical result, network access or submission was approved; those require separately reviewed evidence.

P2R0G18B5C6.title: Static review of the V1R5 refit runtime
P2R0G18B5C6.summary: Audit an acyclic runtime with external inputs bound explicitly before any all-network refit can run.
P2R0G18B5C6.result: The frozen runtime passed independent static review. The associated scientific branch failed cross-validation, so the review permits no live refit, model, package or submission.

P2R0G18B5E3.title: Unreviewed V1R5R1 inference accounting repair
P2R0G18B5E3.summary: Freeze a narrow accounting repair while preserving the preceding inference model.
P2R0G18B5E3.result: The repair received no independent review and was superseded for live use. It supplies no approved model export, resource result or package; reuse requires a newly reviewed successor.

P2R0G18C1.title: One-use production-scope controller
P2R0G18C1.summary: Use an independently reviewed controller to produce the exact scope records for one authorized transaction.
P2R0G18C1.result: The transaction completed and its metadata passed independent review. Its one-use authority is consumed: the result does not authorize another run or the next experimental stage.

P2R0G19B_SUPPLY.title: Improve the supplied K21 pair state
P2R0G19B_SUPPLY.summary: Reduce the error in deep-layer K21 planes, which limit how much of the final prediction error the correction can recover.
P2R0G19B_SUPPLY.result: Offline relative error fell from 8.0% to 6.4%. Estimated planes recovered 15.8% of error versus 54.9% with true planes. The unresolved goal is 2–3% plane error with an affordable implementation.

P2R0G19B_REFIT.title: Refit with collective features from the deployed model
P2R0G19B_REFIT.summary: Add three collective-state features to the F2J correction, computing them from the same model state during training and deployment.
P2R0G19B_REFIT.result: Feature generation was recorded as running on 688 networks. No final refit result is claimed here; success requires a cross-validated improvement and a useful compute-adjusted gain after packaging.

P2R0G19B_MATH_PORTFOLIO_GRAM.title: Three-source nonlinear correction: proof questions
P2R0G19B_MATH_PORTFOLIO_GRAM.summary: Group the separate mathematical claims for a nonlinear correction with three sources.
P2R0G19B_MATH_PORTFOLIO_GRAM.result: This is a workstream index, not an experimental result. Each child claim must be resolved separately; evidence for one does not settle its siblings.

P2R0G19B_MATH_LIE_JORDAN.title: Third-order Lie–Jordan resummation: proof questions
P2R0G19B_MATH_LIE_JORDAN.summary: Group the structural questions for a third-order Lie–Jordan resummation that accounts for interactions between corrections.
P2R0G19B_MATH_LIE_JORDAN.result: This record contains no standalone result. The individual child claims carry their own evidence and remain separately testable.

P2R0G19B_MATH_CAUSAL_PAIR_FIELD.title: Target-adjoint Hankel representation: proof questions
P2R0G19B_MATH_CAUSAL_PAIR_FIELD.summary: Group the structural questions for a minimal Hankel representation of the target-adjoint calculation.
P2R0G19B_MATH_CAUSAL_PAIR_FIELD.result: This is an index to separate mathematical claims, not a validated estimator. Resolving one child does not establish the others.

P2R0G19B_K31_UNIVERSAL_SCALAR_IDENTITY.title: Scalar identity for the mixed fourth cumulant K31
P2R0G19B_K31_UNIVERSAL_SCALAR_IDENTITY.summary: Express the mixed fourth cumulant of centered variables as E[U³V] − 3E[U²]E[UV].
P2R0G19B_K31_UNIVERSAL_SCALAR_IDENTITY.result: The identity is proved for arbitrary centered distributions. It also equals one quarter of the directional derivative of the diagonal fourth-cumulant potential.

P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_MASK_RANK.title: Rank and cost of the final K31 contraction
P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_MASK_RANK.summary: Determine whether the mask used in the actual final-output K31 correction admits a cheap rank-one calculation.
P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_MASK_RANK.result: The mask is generically full rank. The dense 12.3-equivalent contraction is the applicable total-action cost; obtaining a useful residual remains a separate problem.

P2R0G19B_K31_ACTION_COVERAGE.title: Does one K31 scalar preserve the needed correction?
P2R0G19B_K31_ACTION_COVERAGE.summary: A scalar K31 summary discards many tensor directions. Determine whether any discarded direction can change the final Bellman correction.
P2R0G19B_K31_ACTION_COVERAGE.result: Unresolved: prove every discarded direction is invisible to the target and the retained correction meets its error bound, or exhibit a counterexample.

P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_FACTORIZATION.title: Factor final error through local K31 residuals
P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_FACTORIZATION.summary: Test whether local K31 residuals at earlier layers capture final-output information missing from the complete D11 response.
P2R0G19B_K31_ENDPOINT_FACTORIZATION.result: Unresolved: prove the residual row space captures that information after removing existing responses, without hidden work quadratic in depth.

P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_ALIAS_COST_NOGO.title: Existing D14/D10 buffers cannot supply the AQ core
P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_ALIAS_COST_NOGO.summary: Reuse already allocated intermediate buffers to obtain the forward AQ core needed by the correction.
P2R0G19B_K31_AQ_ALIAS_COST_NOGO.result: The buffers do not contain that mathematical object. Reconstructing it exceeds the remaining compute budget, closing this buffer-reuse route; direct scalar interfaces are separate.

P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_COMPLETION.title: Missing higher-order information that affects later layers
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_COMPLETION.summary: Separate additions beyond the D11 fourth-order interface into Z22, AQ cubic-jet, and primitive 211/1111 contributions, each with its own evidence and cost.
P2R0G19B_K31_FUTURE_COMPLETION.result: This is an index to independent mechanisms. Each child must demonstrate information absent from the existing state and account for its own cost.

P2R0G19B_K31_H3_D3_STAR.title: Third-derivative residual beyond the assembled state
P2R0G19B_K31_H3_D3_STAR.summary: Isolate a same-layer third-derivative correction after subtracting the existing third- and fourth-order contributions.
P2R0G19B_K31_H3_D3_STAR.result: The residual is identified algebraically. An exact interface to compute its action, proof that it adds new information and a robust final-error gain are still required.

P2R0G19B_REVERSE_H4_CYCLIC_ESCAPE.title: Target-specific reverse fourth-order state
P2R0G19B_REVERSE_H4_CYCLIC_ESCAPE.summary: Keep only the part of reverse fourth-order propagation that can affect the final output, rather than the full autonomous state.
P2R0G19B_REVERSE_H4_CYCLIC_ESCAPE.result: Unresolved: its rank must fit the compute ceiling and retain more than 96.719% of the target-weighted energy, including error returned through sixth- and eighth-order terms.

P2R0G19B_Q211_FULL_PRODUCT_CLOSURE.title: Complete products required by q211 and H3
P2R0G19B_Q211_FULL_PRODUCT_CLOSURE.summary: List every factor product and collision-square term needed for the complete higher-order reverse calculation.
P2R0G19B_Q211_FULL_PRODUCT_CLOSURE.result: Antisymmetric fusion alone omits required products. Each missing term must be already available, factorizable on the actual source, or proved irrelevant to the final correction.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_AQ_GALERKIN_REPLACEMENT.title: NCQC/AQ replacement for state propagation
P2R0G19B_NCQC_AQ_GALERKIN_REPLACEMENT.summary: Replace the propagated state with symmetric cores that preserve covariance and regenerate third- and fourth-order information through exact AQ ReLU resets.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_AQ_GALERKIN_REPLACEMENT.result: The construction still needs joint initialization, deployment cost, new-information and final-error proofs. Its theorem, provenance, accuracy and value checks remain separate.

P2R0G19B_NCQC_RAW_PARTIAL_CORRELATION.title: Correlation needed to reach raw MSE below 1e-8
P2R0G19B_NCQC_RAW_PARTIAL_CORRELATION.summary: Quantify how well a proposed correction must predict the error left after removing the existing estimator’s response.
P2R0G19B_NCQC_RAW_PARTIAL_CORRELATION.result: Reducing 2.9409e-8 below 1e-8 requires absolute partial correlation above 0.8124. A population covariance certificate is still needed; local reset accuracy does not establish this.

P2R0G19B_RAW_THREE_CHANNEL_CAPACITY.title: Error budget for variance, third and fourth cumulants
P2R0G19B_RAW_THREE_CHANNEL_CAPACITY.summary: Write the remaining error as a weighted contribution from the three correction channels plus their cross-interaction.
P2R0G19B_RAW_THREE_CHANNEL_CAPACITY.result: The algebraic capacity relation is established. It does not produce the required corrections: each channel still needs a valid provider of information missing from the current estimator.

P2R0G19B_Z22_LITERAL_Q22_OWNERSHIP.title: Does the reverse calculation expose the full Q22 state?
P2R0G19B_Z22_LITERAL_Q22_OWNERSHIP.summary: Check whether the full Q22 quantity exists before compression, allowing a direct quadratic-cost contraction.
P2R0G19B_Z22_LITERAL_Q22_OWNERSHIP.result: The current D11 implementation owns only a pairing direction. The full synchronized buffer and its use along every later path remain unproved; the generic rank-dependent cost still applies.

P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_VALUE.title: Final-output value of a two-ray CP4 addition
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_VALUE.summary: Test whether a two-ray CP4 representation adds useful final-output information after accounting for existing responses and the terms it replaces.
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_TWO_RAY_VALUE.result: An exact representation alone is insufficient. The additional correction must survive projection against the existing model and outweigh displaced CP4 value under the error bound.

P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_VALUE.title: Does the auxiliary Clifford identity improve the output?
P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_VALUE.summary: Use a zero-product scalar identity only if the final q211 query lies in the same small chiral subspace.
P2R0G19B_CLIFFORD_AUXILIARY_VALUE.result: Unresolved: prove a nonzero, robust final-output contribution after removing existing responses, while preserving the covariance and third-order providers.

P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_STAR_BIRTH.title: Four-ray CP4 correction with Star4 cancellation
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_STAR_BIRTH.summary: Combine four polarized rays to introduce an AABC term without K22 leakage, then cancel the accompanying K31 leakage with Star4.
P2R0G19B_Q211_CP4_FOUR_RAY_STAR_BIRTH.result: The proposed cancellation is limited to the same site or one transition. Explicit forward amplitudes and directions, plus coordinate-frame verification, are still required.

P2R0G19B_AQ_FUSED_SURFACE_Q211.title: Compute the full AQ q211 reset contribution
P2R0G19B_AQ_FUSED_SURFACE_Q211.summary: Provide explicit connected fourth-order reset-surface contractions instead of assuming a shared eigensystem makes every query available.
P2R0G19B_AQ_FUSED_SURFACE_Q211.result: Unresolved: supply the contractions, collision handling, quadrature error and added cost. Without them, the remaining AQ reset contribution is not supplied.

P2R0G19B_Q211_SURFACE_QUERY_FACTOR_RANK.title: Low-rank factorization of the reverse surface query
P2R0G19B_Q211_SURFACE_QUERY_FACTOR_RANK.summary: Evaluate the signed-surface query without a full tensor, using Tucker or partial-CP factors that remain small through every reverse reset.
P2R0G19B_Q211_SURFACE_QUERY_FACTOR_RANK.result: No stable low-rank bound is established. Generic width-1024 rank returns a query with about 535 million coordinates, so the cheap scalar implementation still needs proof.

P2R0G19B_R54_AFFINE_SEAM_RANK_OBSTRUCTIO.title: Rank obstruction at the r54 affine interface
P2R0G19B_R54_AFFINE_SEAM_RANK_OBSTRUCTIO.summary: Check whether the proposed affine interface can vary all covariance directions while matching the K21 constraints.
P2R0G19B_R54_AFFINE_SEAM_RANK_OBSTRUCTIO.result: It misses exactly 470,935 covariance-normal directions, despite the K21 differential being onto under the stated conditions. The rank obstruction rules out a local section at M = 0.

P2R0G19B_D14_L4_AQ55_STRONG_SEAM.title: Preserve future responses at the D14–AQ interface
P2R0G19B_D14_L4_AQ55_STRONG_SEAM.summary: Join the layer-4 D14 state to the rank-55 AQ state without losing cubic or quartic components that later layers can detect.
P2R0G19B_D14_L4_AQ55_STRONG_SEAM.result: Matching covariance and K21 alone is insufficient. Every discarded component must be matched or proved invisible to the remaining layers; otherwise its mismatch must enter the final-error bound.

P2R0G19B_AQ_R45_HYBRID_FRAME_CANDIDATE.title: AQ hybrid with one frozen frame
P2R0G19B_AQ_R45_HYBRID_FRAME_CANDIDATE.summary: Reduce the cost of the r45 AQ hybrid by reusing one frame rather than recomputing every interior Gram matrix.
P2R0G19B_AQ_R45_HYBRID_FRAME_CANDIDATE.result: The stated subtotal falls from about 49.53 to 48.47, but the flat diagnostic leaves little error margin. The frozen layer, frame mismatch and other approximation errors still need a joint final-error bound.

P2R0G19B_H211_TARGET_WEIGHTED_OPERATOR.title: Low-rank H211 response weighted by the final target
P2R0G19B_H211_TARGET_WEIGHTED_OPERATOR.summary: Compress the response that the final output actually observes, after removing existing responses and accounting for source covariance.
P2R0G19B_H211_TARGET_WEIGHTED_OPERATOR.result: Unweighted local slices do not establish useful low rank. The target-weighted singular-value tail, reverse recurrence, source metric and robust signal still need to meet the applicable rank and cost limits.

P2R0G19B_R48_BELLMAN_SCHUR_QUOTIENT.title: Match only covariance directions needed by the target
P2R0G19B_R48_BELLMAN_SCHUR_QUOTIENT.summary: After matching K21, ask whether the r48 construction can cover the covariance directions that the backward target queries need.
P2R0G19B_R48_BELLMAN_SCHUR_QUOTIENT.result: Only 155,648 of 476,776 covariance-normal dimensions are accessible. It remains to prove that the needed target subspace fits inside them with stable conditioning and without per-network fitting.

P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SURFACE_FUSION.title: Share fourth-order surface work with the final six resets
P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SURFACE_FUSION.summary: Reuse already paid eigensystems and quadrature nodes when adding a connected fourth-order surface to the six-reset suffix.
P2R0G19B_D14_L8_AQ55_SURFACE_FUSION.result: A common diagonal latent slice may fit the budget; a generic dense r55 surface does not. The shared frame or low-rank structure, exact collision handling and full added cost remain to be proved.

P2R0G19B_AQ_RANK_WINDOW_VERONESE_COST_FR.title: AQ rank, missing directions and suffix cost
P2R0G19B_AQ_RANK_WINDOW_VERONESE_COST_FR.summary: Calculate how increasing AQ rank reduces first-order directions that the representation cannot capture, and how that changes affordable suffix depth.
P2R0G19B_AQ_RANK_WINDOW_VERONESE_COST_FR.result: The missing dimension falls from 4,656 at rank 61 to 561 at rank 62 and zero at rank 63. This is a rank/cost result only; initialization, a cubic solution and final-output value are not established.

P2R0G19B_AQ_H4_SQUARE_STEIN_KERNEL_IDENT.title: Fourth-order AQ square as a Stein discrepancy
P2R0G19B_AQ_H4_SQUARE_STEIN_KERNEL_IDENT.summary: Express the symmetric Stein matrix’s difference from covariance using explicit first- and second-order features of the AQ cores.
P2R0G19B_AQ_H4_SQUARE_STEIN_KERNEL_IDENT.result: The finite noncommutative identity is exact, and its covariance recovers all three fourth-order pairings. It does not provide a cheap contraction with a later-layer Hessian.

P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_GRAM_GATE.title: Positive-Gram test for the r63 first-order interface
P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_GRAM_GATE.summary: Replace an explicit right-inverse construction with a Gram-matrix test for whether the proposed interface can realize all required first-order changes.
P2R0G19B_R63_FIRST_ORDER_GRAM_GATE.result: The equivalence is established, but a positive Gram at the actual network cut and a lower singular-value bound are still missing. Surjectivity of one component alone is insufficient.

P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_K21_DUAL_GATE.title: Generic K21 surjectivity for CP4-seeded AQ63
P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_K21_DUAL_GATE.summary: Determine whether the CP4-seeded construction can vary every oriented K21 direction along its constrained tangent space.
P2R0G19B_CP4_SEEDED_AQ63_K21_DUAL_GATE.result: A generic mathematical theorem proves surjectivity for widths up to 1,954, including 1,024. Computing a valid section and matching everything later layers need remain separate tasks.

P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SILENT_GRAM_CERTIFICA.title: A 561-dimensional Gram test for the r62 cubic equation
P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SILENT_GRAM_CERTIFICA.summary: Restrict to variations that leave the tangent constraints unchanged, reducing cubic surjectivity to a finite Gram-matrix test.
P2R0G19B_R62_CUBIC_SILENT_GRAM_CERTIFICA.result: The exact reduction uses a 561 × 561 Gram matrix. No positive instance at the actual network cut is yet known, so the certificate is a test to apply, not an implemented solution.

P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_RESIDENCY_GATE.title: Missing weighted trace row in the reverse state
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_RESIDENCY_GATE.summary: Check whether the existing D10/D11 reverse state already contains the weighted trace row required by the Price calculation.
P2R0G19B_AQ_PRICE_TRACE_RESIDENCY_GATE.result: It does not declare that row or a reverse q211 lifetime. A deployable contraction must supply the full future query or factor it through existing pair state, including the cost of acquiring missing information.

P2R0G19B_GAUSSIAN_Q211_CP3_JET_IDENTITY.title: Gaussian q211 from derivatives of the CP3 surface
P2R0G19B_GAUSSIAN_Q211_CP3_JET_IDENTITY.summary: Express connected q211 at arbitrary thresholds using a threshold derivative of the third cumulant plus explicit one- and two-variable terms.
P2R0G19B_GAUSSIAN_Q211_CP3_JET_IDENTITY.result: The analytic identity is exact, with a first/second latent-mean derivative extension for quadratic AQ. Knowing the CP3 value alone does not supply those derivatives.

P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_BIASED_CHANNEL_RANK_GA.title: Bias can require three independent q211 product channels
P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_BIASED_CHANNEL_RANK_GA.summary: Determine how many product channels survive after subtracting the finite D11 state when the network has arbitrary bias.
P2R0G19B_Q211_K22_BIASED_CHANNEL_RANK_GA.result: The generic quotient has three independent channels, approaching 90 unfused products. A cheaper route needs a zero-bias argument, a controlled bias remainder or a proved rank-one fusion; cost and value then need rechecking.

P2R0G19B_AQ_Q4_Q3SQUARED_CANCELLATION.title: Squared third cumulant changes the fourth-order response
P2R0G19B_AQ_Q4_Q3SQUARED_CANCELLATION.summary: Include the squared third-cumulant term when calculating the local zero-bias mean and variance corrections.
P2R0G19B_AQ_Q4_Q3SQUARED_CANCELLATION.result: The response depends on the difference between fourth cumulant and squared third cumulant. The identity and cancellation bounds are proved locally; actual bias, existing-state overlap and final-output effects remain separate.

P2R0G19B_AQ_R62_QONLY_COST_RECEIPT.title: Five-reset r62 Q-only cost subtotal
P2R0G19B_AQ_R62_QONLY_COST_RECEIPT.summary: Count the Q-only work for five resets and check how much computation remains for additional matrix operations.
P2R0G19B_AQ_R62_QONLY_COST_RECEIPT.result: The subtotal leaves insufficient room for a second width-1,953 Gram matrix. This arithmetic excludes interface construction, source acquisition, distributional validity and final-output value.

P2R0G19B_TRUE_MINUS_AQ_DIRECTIONAL_L4_RE.title: Directional fourth moment needed for a true-minus-AQ bound
P2R0G19B_TRUE_MINUS_AQ_DIRECTIONAL_L4_RE.summary: Identify the exact fourth-order directional information needed to bound the difference between the true state and its AQ approximation.
P2R0G19B_TRUE_MINUS_AQ_DIRECTIONAL_L4_RE.result: The required signed fourth-moment information and a safe derivative-based bound are characterized. This is an oracle/identifiability result, not evidence that the existing implementation can provide the information.

P2R0G19B_ANALYTIC_RSS_INDEPENDENCE_NOGO.title: Why independent Gaussian draws do not justify RSS error bounds
P2R0G19B_ANALYTIC_RSS_INDEPENDENCE_NOGO.summary: Test whether fresh Gaussian independence allows deterministic approximation errors to be combined by root-sum-square.
P2R0G19B_ANALYTIC_RSS_INDEPENDENCE_NOGO.result: It does not. Analytically integrated truncation creates conditional bias, not a centered fresh error. Root-sum-square needs conditional centering and a fixed, past-measurable target pullback.

P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_FORWARD_REPLA.title: Common-radial mixture for the forward pair reset
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_FORWARD_REPLA.summary: Replace the Q24 pair reset with Gaussian ReLU moments averaged over a common radial scale, using total covariance and the existing quadratic Gram.
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_MIXTURE_FORWARD_REPLA.result: Means and covariance are computed together, avoiding a reverse tape. The proposal still needs positive-semidefinite synchronization, a finite-matrix model-error bound, proof of new information and a final-MSE gain.

P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_CENTERED_COLLECTIVE_C.title: Centered radial novelty is only rank one
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_CENTERED_COLLECTIVE_C.summary: Subtract the existing covariance response from the centered pure radial model to see what new variation remains.
P2R0G19B_AQ_RADIAL_CENTERED_COLLECTIVE_C.result: The residual is exactly a collective rank-one form, with leading coefficient −6/r². It cannot explain the broad variance channel in this centered case; noncollective value needs bias, an affine part or later nonlinear mixing.

P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_SUBSPACE_COMPRESSED_.title: Target-sized Gram test for r63
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_SUBSPACE_COMPRESSED_.summary: Test only the final-output directions of interest rather than demanding a solution for every possible state direction.
P2R0G19B_R63_TARGET_SUBSPACE_COMPRESSED_.result: Positive definiteness of the q × q compressed Gram is necessary and sufficient at first order for those q directions. Computing and conditioning this matrix at the actual cut remain unresolved.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_FINITE_JET_SECTION_NOGO.title: No universal finite-polynomial solution for AQ63
P2R0G19B_AQ63_FINITE_JET_SECTION_NOGO.summary: Ask whether a finite polynomial or finite Taylor expansion can exactly invert the coupled cubic K21 relation.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_FINITE_JET_SECTION_NOGO.result: Even the scalar restriction has nonzero inverse coefficients at arbitrarily high odd orders, ruling out a universal finite polynomial solution. A selected cubic-null range or nonpolynomial primitive remains possible.

P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_EXCEPTIONAL_SPE.title: Exceptional cubic-null subspace for AQ63
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_EXCEPTIONAL_SPE.summary: Seek a special subspace of dimension at least 1,023 that avoids the generic cubic obstruction and admits a cheap solution.
P2R0G19B_AQ63_CUBIC_NULL_EXCEPTIONAL_SPE.result: No construction with the required spectral and anticommutant properties is known. Nor is there an unconditional dimension bound ruling it out. Either a valid construction or a stronger impossibility proof is needed.

P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_ZERO_BIAS_.title: Zero-bias action from existing K31 and K21 planes
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_ZERO_BIAS_.summary: Write the broad completion action in terms of diagonal rescalings of already available K31, K21 and covariance quantities.
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_ZERO_BIAS_.result: The zero-bias formula is exact for every correlation, and the interior H7/H9 terms vanish by parity. Nonzero means introduce additional derivative terms that this result does not cover.

P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_VARIANCE_L.title: Variance correction alone falls short of the target
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_VARIANCE_L.summary: Compare the total error reduction attributable to the certified variance channel with the threshold for proceeding and the final accuracy target.
P2R0G19B_AQ_OWNED_EXPONENTIAL_VARIANCE_L.result: Even perfect recovery of the 17.46% variance contribution misses the 20% threshold and the roughly 66% reduction needed for raw MSE below 1e-8. Additional effects or controlled amplification are required.

P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_RAW_VALUE_GATE.title: Does the mixed L6 source reduce final error?
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_RAW_VALUE_GATE.summary: Test whether the inexpensive mixed source predicts errors that remain after correcting defects and subtracting the existing estimator’s response.
P2R0G19B_AQ_SHARED_Z_L6_RAW_VALUE_GATE.result: Its useful final-output alignment is unknown. Held-out gain and a combined model/remainder error bound sufficient for MSE below 1e-8 are still required.

P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_SOURCE_COLLISION_OWN.title: Account for repeated-index terms in trace q211
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_SOURCE_COLLISION_OWN.summary: Check that the lower-order terms needed when source indices coincide are available at the same layer and normalization.
P2R0G19B_Q211_TRACE_SOURCE_COLLISION_OWN.result: The one-product identity applies to the completed tensor. Excluding repeated indices is free only if the corresponding K31, K22 and K4 terms already exist; otherwise their acquisition and residual effect must be counted.

P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_OLD_SCHUR_GA.title: Does trace q211 add information beyond the current model?
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_OLD_SCHUR_GA.summary: Assemble the pairing, collision, propagation and higher-order terms at one layer before subtracting the existing model’s complete response.
P2R0G19B_Q211_LEADING_TRACE_OLD_SCHUR_GA.result: A nonzero remaining feature, useful signed effect on final error and a bound on the omitted higher-order tail are still needed. The trace scalar alone does not establish a usable correction.

P2R0G19B_Q211_DRD_LEAF_TWO_PRODUCT_IDENT.title: Structured q211 pullback in two matrix products
P2R0G19B_Q211_DRD_LEAF_TWO_PRODUCT_IDENT.summary: Exploit the form P = Diag(u) R Diag(u) when evaluating the exact reverse action.
P2R0G19B_Q211_DRD_LEAF_TWO_PRODUCT_IDENT.result: This structure needs two dense matrix products plus reductions; a generic dense P retains the qualified three-product calculation. Collision terms and final-query rank still require separate treatment.

P2R0G19B_R55_RAW_STABILIZER_969_MINOR.title: Full rank of the raw r55 stabilizer block
P2R0G19B_R55_RAW_STABILIZER_969_MINOR.summary: Construct an explicit 903 + 66 minor, including the input-action term omitted in the earlier calculation.
P2R0G19B_R55_RAW_STABILIZER_969_MINOR.result: The raw stabilizer block has full rank 969. This does not yet show that the rank survives elimination of the symmetric block.

P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_SOURCE_ARITY.title: Three-Hessian identity covers only one residual factor
P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_SOURCE_ARITY.summary: Determine which true-minus-AQ terms the three-Hessian formula actually computes.
P2R0G19B_H211_THREE_HESSIAN_SOURCE_ARITY.result: With the AQ surface it duplicates existing work; with a tilted residual surface it covers only terms containing one residual factor. Terms with two or more need their own directional fourth-moment information.

P2R0G19B_QHEAD_DIRECT_TRANSPOSE.title: Direct-transpose correction failed its accuracy check
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_DIRECT_TRANSPOSE.summary: Turn the direct-transpose source on and off to measure its effect on both local q error and final mean error.
P2R0G19B_QHEAD_DIRECT_TRANSPOSE.result: Both became slightly worse. Final MSE rose from 3.033159e-8 to 3.033604e-8, so the exact tested correction was rejected.

P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_H4_AUDIT.title: Static audit of the H4 test runner
P2R0G19B_OWNED_L3_L3SQUARE_H4_AUDIT.summary: Independently review the test runner’s control logic without accessing targets, cached rows or training data.
