S1LR (2026-09-24) computes the star's dense product s1 = pw w from the rank-32 factors too (native bill ~-2.1%, raw +0.43%). The porter's 'lrnys' variant replaces A Omega by a gather of the 48 largest-norm columns (test only).

terms.label: LVFS / lvfuse_sized32
terms.meaning: Fuse every left-operand tree, and fuse right-operand/output trees only when their size is at most _LVFS_LIMIT. The original limit is 32_000_000 floats. Larger right/output trees use per-component operations. This threshold is a tree element-count limit, not a request-count limit; the source states identical operation order, predictions, and bill.

terms.label: m2 / qb / eold / qold (learned-head physical features)
terms.meaning: The added head features are: m2 = t3^2 He4(alpha) phi(alpha)/72, the second-order mean term divided by sigma; qb = the off-diagonal read plane contracted against c = (gate/sigma)^2 mu, then normalized by (c dot mu - c_i mu_i) v_i; eold = sum_r |lambda_r| pp_ir^2/v_i over cohorts aged at least three layers; qold = their uncentered local quartic divided by v_i^2. The record uses these as features supplied to learned heads. Lowercase m2 here is distinct from the W^2 message M2.

terms.label: mean formula
terms.meaning: The card's per-unit post-ReLU mean: m = mg + k3*e/6 + k4*f/24, where mg = sigma*(a*Phi(a) + phi(a)) is the Gaussian term (a = mu/sigma), e = -a*phi(a)/v is the third-cumulant sensitivity and f the fourth-cumulant term ((a^2-1)*phi(a)-type); i.e. the Gaussian ReLU mean plus Gram-Charlier/Edgeworth tilts from the unit's own skew and kurtosis. Its inputs are the per-unit mean, variance, skew and kurtosis; fed true inputs it is accurate to the Monte Carlo noise floor.

terms.label: micro-stack (flat-dial parabola optima, #337212)
terms.meaning: The 2026-10-19 release stack of zero-bill dial moves read at predict time, each set at the vertex of its parabola on the store ranks: _S19_K4BAND (0.9826, 0.9812, 0.9613), _NP_K3L_BY_LAYER (per-layer three K31L4 strengths), _K31R_TABLE (0.5426, 0.5027) at every layer, _K4L_C (0.814, 0.676), the _NP_STRENGTH table and _BSK 0.434; graded as #337212 (1.4296e-9, -0.225%).

terms.label: MX1 / MX2 / MX3
terms.meaning: These terms contain a hub's second derivative, two carried third-cumulant legs, and one Gaussian covariance edge, exemplified by d_a kappa3(z_a,z_b,z_c) g_b g_c g_d C_ad. MX1 requires theta_ri = 6 sum_a d_a pp_ra E_ai Y_ai, a contraction over hubs and bank columns. The research distinguishes this family from the pair-local norm-coupling law and local fourth-chaos term.

terms.label: NCAR
terms.meaning: For iid Gaussian weights the fourth cumulant of a layer's pre-activations has a second-chaos part carried by one matrix, Ntilde_ij = sum_k kappa4(z_i, z_j, z_k, z_k) (how the covariance of a pair moves with the layer's squared norm), whose network-specific part is mostly top covariance eigenvectors x per-unit partner vectors. NCAR carried the partner vectors q_m from layer to layer with matrix-vector products and added (3/n) Ntilde as an extra K31 plane (-4% on held-out 651). Superseded 2026-10-02 12:54Z by the pair-carried law NCAR6.

terms.label: NCAR6 (pair-carried law, pair law, NP)
terms.meaning: The whole lean law of the norm-coupling matrix carried on the bank's own column pairs: each hub's fresh source is a symmetric 2x2 form [[S2, rv], [rv, D]] on its pair (s, e) (births, row forms, diagonal), carried as one weight w_r per bank column plus one cross weight x_h per pair and transported by the bank's own push, gates and joins. It is folded into the K21 bank read: diagB_i = sum_r (w_r pp_ir^2 + x_r pp_ir pp_partner), a regression of diagB on (tr C v_i, mu_i^2, 2 mu_i (C mu)_i) gives the multiple of C to remove (aB), the read's left factor becomes pp^2 lam + f (w pp + x pp_partner) with f_i = -strength mu_i/(n v_i), and plane_ij -= f_i aB C_ij off the diagonal. Native lever NP (a38, v9: every per-unit and per-hub formula is one polynomial evaluation from constant tables built at import; switches _NP_FORMS = which forms the fold removes, _NP_DFIT = the regression with a constant in place of the table, _NP_BETA = the carried weights from the card's beta, _NP_K3L = the K31L4 term). -14.4% on held-out 651 (torch), -5.6..-7.5% pooled; fired as S40 (#333559, third place).

terms.label: NP strength (_NP_STRENGTH)
terms.meaning: The per-layer strength of the pair-carried law's fold in the bank read (the NP lever); the first joint dial solve set it to 1.83/1.40/1.18 by layer band (S41), the table in the file runs 1.82 at layer 1 down to ~1.01 late; x0.97 was -0.1% on the base file but did not transfer to the readout stack.

terms.label: NT join
terms.meaning: Static Nystrom oversampled by p extra rows (p32/p64/p128) followed by an eigen-truncation back to rank 384; it captures the whole join prize (-1.30% MSE natively = the no-join ceiling -1.55%) but trades about 1:1 with bill (rates 0.64-1.14). Closed 2026-10-16.

terms.label: Nystrom join
terms.meaning: The sketch used at the joins since S23: the rows with the largest Gram diagonal are the pivots, Y = G[:, rows], then QR; the basis is the column space of a column subset of the Gram. Under the Winograd kernels' rounding (4-8e-6 relative) this one-product sketch is noise-optimal: power steps, whitening, oversampling with eigen-truncation (NT) and random or value-weighted pivots were all measured worse or 1:1 with bill.

terms.label: O18 / O20 switches (_O18PAD_RULES, _O18_REQUEST_PENALTY, _O20_GRAM_ON, _O20_MU32/_O20_B32, _O20_ECUT_RADICAL)
terms.meaning: _O18PAD_RULES pads some products up to kernel-eligible shapes (nominally more work, fewer metered multiplies); _O18_REQUEST_PENALTY = 2,000,000 is the metered FLOPs a route must save per added request to be selected among exact routes; _O20_GRAM_ON computes only the upper half of symmetric Gram products; _O20_MU32 / _O20_B32 use float32 instead of float64 for the mean and b-carrier transports; _O20_ECUT_RADICAL_* replaces the edge cut's tanh by a rational nonlinearity (a measured approximation).

terms.label: OTT (old positive tail)
terms.meaning: An approximation of the old tier's positive-tail diagonal by the Gaussian first-chaos trace: only the local reconstruction of old rows beyond the tail threshold _OTT_Z = 2.5 is cut, the complete carried tensor is unchanged. The L14 exactness stack raises the threshold to _OTT14_Z = 3.0 at the L14 push only ('old-tail positive side 3.0': raw -0.15% for ~+0.09% bill); the exact version (OTT off, all old rows exact) is worth -0.32% for +2.8% bill.

terms.label: pad18
terms.meaning: A whitelist maps eighteen observed matrix-product shapes to padded shapes under the recorded flopscope price model. It applies to ordinary products and one shared-old384 product. The source introduces local temporary arrays and retains the parent dispatcher's cache policy.

terms.label: pair map
terms.meaning: The card's bivariate step (the function nonlinear(mu, C, K21, k4, ...) in the file): from a layer's pre-activation mean, covariance and third/fourth-order inputs it produces the post-ReLU mean, the post covariance (a Mehler/Price series in the pair correlation truncated at rho^3, plus Gram-Charlier terms from K21, K31 and K22) and the radial coefficient. About 1-2% of the bill.

terms.label: pe3 / pe4
terms.meaning: Per-layer dial families added to the refit line at S54: multipliers (1 + pe3[l]) and (1 + pe4[l]) on the pair map's local skew and kurtosis terms e3 and e4 (via t3 / t4), which appear only in the pair map; natively _PE34_BY_LAYER.

terms.label: peel / shared / fusion budgets (level fusion)
terms.meaning: Route-selection budgets of the kernel planner. Peel = exact depth peeling: a product is split so that an exact Smirnov L6 body (families such as peel6_p20_4_4_17) handles the main block and the fringe goes to the incumbent kernel ('fixed public-tariff strict750 mixed fringe policy'; plans _PEEL_PUSH_PLANS / _PEEL_READ_PLANS selected only by the saved public weighted arithmetic tariff, -0.73% bill on the matched census); shared = one operand's transform reused across products (the shared _SMX_ENV arena); level fusion = tree levels / chunk keys fused so fewer requests are issued ('restricted level fusion' = left-operand trees only: bill 0, bytes identical, kernel time -13%). Each route is chosen by metered FLOPs saved per added request (_O18_REQUEST_PENALTY).

terms.label: plane
terms.meaning: A matrix-valued cumulant slice of a layer indexed by unit pairs: the (2,1) plane K21, the (3,1) plane K31, the (2,2) plane K22. 'The plane' alone usually means the K21 plane the pair map reads; 'plane content' or 'plane error' is the part of the final error attributable to the planes (the leaders' gap).

terms.label: plane bank (bank of columns)
terms.meaning: The card's representation of the third-order cumulant tensor: a set of symmetric rank-one columns p_r with weights lam_r, two columns born per kink (hub) unit at each layer and pushed through W at every later layer, with the old cohorts compressed into rank-384 frames at layers 7, 10 and 13. About 80% of the bill (push ~43%, read ~35%). Not to be confused with 'bank' = a graded submission that became the best public score.

terms.label: power-step sketch
terms.meaning: A refinement of the join sketch: one power iteration Y = G1 Y1 on the Gram of a column subsample, closing 60-80% of the join-basis gap offline. It failed natively (+28% MSE) because the step squares the spectrum and float32 plus kernel rounding destroy the trailing directions; whitened variants stayed 2.5-4x worse than Nystrom. Closed 2026-10-17.

terms.label: prebind / prebinding / _PB_WALL_S / lazy bind
terms.meaning: Binding the fixed-shape frames and arena views of the Winograd trees in setup (Estimator.setup runs once per worker outside every predict's budget; the platform books it as setup_executions) so that predict pays no binding requests: a cold network otherwise binds ~219 alt-basis tree cache entries (~22 view requests each). Tree keys are network-specific but recur: a key census over 8 selection networks found 609 distinct keys, the 358 used by at least two cover 62-76% of a held-out network's keys; they are bound most frequent first until _PB_WALL_S (2.8-3.0 s) runs out, then each cache is re-ordered so the most frequent keys are evicted last (predictions unchanged; a cold network's bill falls ~1.7%). A lazy bind is a key setup did not bind, sliced for free from a maximal setup 'box' (fragment_lazybind) or bound at first use inside predict, costing requests and residual on cold networks.

terms.label: proxy-to-hosted transfer
terms.meaning: The ratio of the hosted public-score change to the local (proxy) change: ~0.5 for readout fits (hosted tracks the held-25 pooled number); product-size bill cuts transfer in full, lazy-bind/prebind cuts about half; raw-driven physics pieces transferred at 0 to 3/4.

terms.label: public / private split / designation
terms.meaning: Each run grades 100 networks; the public board shows the mean over evaluation indices 0-49 (so every worker's cold first network is public), the other 50 are hidden; the private re-evaluation scores the designated submissions on a fresh private suite (two designations: #337641 and #337619).

terms.label: push
terms.meaning: Transporting the bank's columns (and the covariance, star and b carrier) through the next weight matrix, pp = W^T p, which is exact; the bank push is the largest bill item (43-44%: young roster pushes ~33%, old-tier reconstruct ~10%).

terms.label: push share / read share
terms.meaning: The fractions of the bill spent on pushing the bank columns (43-44%) and reading the plane out of them (34-35%); the two together, ~80%, are the third-order plane bank, which is why the leaders' lower bill is read as a different third-order representation.

terms.label: pushSM
terms.meaning: A use of the grouped Smirnov kernel family for the matrix products that transport bank columns. The record treats push-Smirnov separately from the adopted young-read plans and records it as held after wall-cost testing.

terms.label: QL / quarterload
terms.meaning: The parent loader copies four natural quadrants, then overwrites one quadrant with a sum or difference. QL copies the other three quadrants and computes that operation from the untouched input, under explicit float32 and shape checks. It changes loading, not rank or arithmetic. _ASTRA_QL_ON is false in the designated file after the later override.

terms.label: RAD (refit line S51-S63)
terms.meaning: The refit-after-drop pipeline: after a bill cut ('drop') the learned arrays and per-layer dial families (ds, pe3, pe4, k21k) are re-fitted on the current card with exact gradients, a point (.pt) is frozen before any check, and the port loop (chain_rad_port) builds the native file; a round's CHECK compares the frozen point against the unrefitted card on fresh networks. Its first round (MS, 2026-10-11) was a null ablation of the carrier strengths; the automated line S51-S63 ran unattended from 2026-10-12 at about one round per 8-10 h (-0.2..-0.4% per round), stopped to 2 workers after two dry rounds (S60).

terms.label: read (bank read / plane read / young read)
terms.meaning: Contracting the pushed columns into the plane the pair map needs on the layer's response rows x live columns (the K21 read: sum_r lam_r pp_ir^2 pp_jr); the 'young read' is the read of the young cohorts' columns (done by the Smirnov grouped kernels), the old tier's read is an inner product in the frame. Second-largest bill item (~35%).

terms.label: readout (on-policy second-step readout)
terms.meaning: A per-layer linear correction of the means fitted by ridge regression on captures of the deployed estimator's own trajectory: the parent file (#337506 source) was run on 90 fresh training networks (TRAIN90), per-layer features captured, and a 961-column ridge fit per layer (ridge 0.03, damping 0.5, five TRAIN72/held-18 folds with seals before the held sets) exported as float32 head rows 1..15 plus one _gop2_gnn_step override. 'On-policy' = fitted on the deployed file's own trajectory rather than off-policy captures. Hosted: -0.40% (#337565, 705 columns), then -0.12% (hg) and -0.11% (fh); the learning curve saturates at ~-1.15% proxy.

terms.label: readout feature blocks (first128, gate design 705, hg, fh, hgfh, 961 columns)
terms.meaning: The linear design has 321 columns: state64 + intercept1 + second hidden128 + first hidden128. Adding elementwise squares of the two hidden layers gives 577 columns; first-hidden x gate gives the 705-column gate design. The hg block adds second-hidden x gate (128), and fh adds the elementwise product of the first and second hidden activations (128), giving 961 columns. These hidden vectors belong to the per-unit learned correction; first128 does not select the first 128 units of the 1024-wide network. The final implementation saves first90 = h before the second encoder layer and computes first90 * h afterward.

terms.label: refit / joint refit (jmB..jmI) / refit base / co-adaptation
terms.meaning: A refit re-fits the learned parameters (arrays, heads, dials) on the current card; a joint refit solves several live arms at once (learned arrays, head columns 6/17/20, m2/eold/qb, qold, kappa_C) with sizes by least squares on 16 line-search ranks and a forward judge on 48 held-out ranks (jmC -0.99%, jmI -0.82%; S44/S45). The refit base is the physics base a refit runs on. Co-adaptation: the learned parts and dials are fitted to the card's own biases, so single truth-ward physics changes do little or hurt, a refit does not buy back a rank cut, and base-file dial wins vanish on the readout stack.

terms.label: release gates (stage A / C / D, prefire, setup5)
terms.meaning: The release lane's qualification gates before a fire: stage A = einsum-signature audit and compile check (no new operation signatures), stage C = boundary legs (projected wall, residual, request counts), stage D = memory and handles (RSS, footprint, handle count), prefire = the import audit, setup5 = the 5-worker setup timing; run by release/lead_chain.sh and later release_min_v1.sh.

terms.label: request / put / request diet / byte-identical
terms.meaning: A request is one client-server round trip of the flopscope client (each operation, each handle fetch); a put is a data upload. The request diet is the set of rewrites that issue fewer requests for the same arithmetic: 'byte-identical' (bit-identical) rewrites keep the predictions bit for bit (e.g. fnp.split returns all column blocks in one request), while 'rounding-level' rewrites change the float order and need ten networks to judge. Caps of the release lane after S40: first network <= 43,800 requests, warm <= 42,700.

terms.label: residual (residual time)
terms.meaning: The per-network client-side time of the participant's Python not covered by metered kernels, capped at 0.4 s by the rules; it is driven by the number of flopscope requests (~16 us local, ~1.4x on the platform per request; ~45K instructions per request) and by sync points and garbage-collector pauses; the designated files run at ~0.35-0.37 s max.

terms.label: response rows / live columns / alive mask
terms.meaning: The rosters of a layer's read: the response rows are the units for which the plane is computed (min(g, 1-g) above the response floor; 1,024 at layers 1-2, ~600-700 at layers 12-14, 544 at L14 on rank 35), the live (alive) columns are the units whose bank columns are kept (gate above the alive floor; 768 at L14), and the alive mask gates the carried columns; the read is a product of shape response rows x live columns x bank columns.

terms.label: RLF
terms.meaning: Sum the old-tier trailing read and the young-tier read in the existing depth-6 leaf basis, then perform one common output unwind. The code states exact real arithmetic but changed float32 arithmetic; it does not reduce rank or concatenate operands.

terms.label: roster
terms.meaning: The index set of units a step keeps (response rows, live columns, births, dead-cut rows), rounded up to multiples of 32 or 64 so the products hit the fixed kernel shapes. Roster sizes are the only client-side scalars the file pulls from the meter. Exact rosters were measured dead: the ~15 padding units per roster carry ~2.3% of the accuracy.

terms.label: row cut (L15 row cut, _L15_ROWCUT_Z, row-cut z)
terms.meaning: At the terminal layer the k3 push and the star diagonal run only on rows with |mu/sigma| <= z (the rest get k3 = 0), because the k3 sensitivity of the output row, -z phi(z)/(6v), vanishes beyond |z| ~ 3 (fable-physicist LG-4, build_l15_rowcut.py). z = 3.5 in the fragment (line 3993), 3.0 in the designated files (line 24554; fired as #337090, -0.30% adjusted); z 2.5 is a cliff (+4.7% MSE). The scored row is the final-layer post mean m = mg + k3 e/6 + k4 f/24.

terms.label: RRPI
terms.meaning: The research parent identified as hill_climb_pair_rr_inverse_v1/candidate.py with source hash prefix a3efb3a1. October 1 comparisons use this parent and its learned parameters. The folder name identifies a pair representation and inverse variant, but does not establish a unique literal expansion of RRPI.

terms.label: RTT (response-row floor of the read)
terms.meaning: The floor z on the rows the young read computes (response rows |mu/sigma| <= z, the rest completed by a rank-2 band); z 1.5 is a sharp optimum: 1.25 costs raw +2.06% for bill -0.31%, 1.75 / 2.0 give raw -0.8% for +1.6..+2.5% bill; the exact prefix variants (RTT2 off: READR -0.17% for +2.2%) do not pay.

terms.label: S2tr
terms.meaning: The 2026-10-15/16 base file of the lineage (the 'S2' release with the trimmed Smirnov plans) used as the shared control (ctl_s2tr) of the October 16 hunts on 8 noise-free seeds 7103248-55 and the 32 store ranks. Inferred from its use as the control name.

terms.label: sandwich / full sandwich / two-strip / _GSAFE5_LIMIT
terms.meaning: A sandwich is a covariance product W^T (C W); a 'full sandwich' is done as one tree product (-315 requests a layer for +1.95% FLOPs); two-strip splits it in two strips (-6.5% of requests for +0.67% FLOPs); _GSAFE5_LIMIT is the number of the five full sandwiches kept (0 after the round-2 diet funded it: -0.47% bill).

terms.label: scale mode (scale mixture)
terms.meaning: The gain mode seen as a rigid scale mixture: conditional second moments respond to the squared norm of an earlier layer with elasticity ~0.5 for means and 0.8-1.0 for variances and covariances, so Sym(C x b) has the right structure; 'the scale mode's column' is the direction the b6 read compares the plane against.

terms.label: seal
terms.meaning: A frozen candidate file with fitted coefficients exported into it (e.g. the on-policy readout seal at strength x1.35, seal_s1.35/candidate_first128_onpolicy_blocks_release_v1.py, with EXPORTED_v1.json recording parents, coefficients and the step override); 'seals before the held sets' means the coefficients are frozen before the held-out folds are scored. Stacks are built on a seal.

terms.label: setup / setup5 / SETUP_TIMEOUT
terms.meaning: setup(context) runs once per worker before any predict, outside any BudgetContext, and is limited to 5 s including the import (SETUP_TIMEOUT fails the whole submission); the file spends it prebinding fixed-shape frames, view aliasing, Smirnov plan preparation and constant tables (~14.8k requests, 4.10-4.26 s on the hosted graders, 3.3-3.5 s locally); #337614 lost one worker to SETUP_TIMEOUT. setup5 is the local release gate that times setup on 5 workers.

terms.label: shared-384 / old384 / _shared_old384_mm
terms.meaning: 'Shared old384 state' is the old tier's shared rank-384 frame (frame Q, the weighted Gram core, the signed column roster) that all joined cohorts live in; _shared_old384_push / _shared_old384_mm are the push and the fast-kernel matrix product routines of that tier (the Winograd/Strassen tree route; each kernel product costs ~70 requests), which the retired fast-rescue governor would have made fall back to its parent route. Inferred from the function names and their call sites.

terms.label: SM40 / Smirnov plan / _ASTRA_SM40_PLANS / _SM40_CAP / size-8e9 drop
terms.meaning: The Smirnov young-read dispatch ('exact rank40 read circuit, over owner-qualified incumbent scratch views'): _ASTRA_SM40_PLANS maps a product shape to a prepared grouped-read plan from view families such as L6_other (6, 10, 5, 29, 5), L5_wide20 (5, 20, 11, 54, 10) and L5_narrow20, prebound at setup (the 'table167' = 167 keys); _SM40_CAP = 4 caps the Smirnov reads per predict (a dict wrapper whose get returns None once _ASTRA_SM40_STATS['calls'] >= the cap, so the dispatcher falls back to the parent read); the size-8e9 drop removes the 9 plans with m*k*n >= 8.0e9. Together they are the wall-margin tail of #337619/#337641 (lines 25700-25710): bill +0.18%, raw unchanged, hosted wall -5 to -6%. SM40 off at import fails setup.

terms.label: Smirnov (grouped reads)
terms.meaning: The grouped strided-read kernel family: reads of the third-order plane bank executed as grouped/batched leaf products over strided views ('3x6x3 L5', '3x3x6 L5' executables at depth L4/L5/L6, packets P10-P40), which save FLOPs (40-560 MF per read) but cost 2-4x the incumbent's server instructions. Variants: SM40 (the young-read plan table), push-Smirnov (held), join/old-bank Smirnov (wall-infeasible), SMX (the shared dispatch).

terms.label: SMX
terms.meaning: The shared Smirnov dispatch API banked 2026-10-16: one _SMX_ON flag (part of the governor's EXACT set), _smx_register / _smx_fits / _smx_call, a lazy binder with view families from arena offset 0, flat outer/padding buffers, and signed executables (_SMX_RECORDS); itself a wall optimisation (off: wall +11.6%, adjusted +0.5%).

terms.label: SS beta (_SS_BETA)
terms.meaning: The per-layer strength of the star-direction fragment (fragment_star_dir_v1; 'the trainer's beta at the star's layer l is _SS_BETA[l-1]'): the live star is one-direction (_SS_RANK = -1 at every layer, line 13531) with strength _SS_BETA, 0.9105 in the fragment and 0.85 in the designated files (opus-solo zb4 stack, line 19839); 0.80 / 0.90 closed as worse or flat.

terms.label: stack / tail
terms.meaning: A stack is a candidate built by appending modifications (tails) to a parent seal or fired file; a tail is an appended block of Python that overrides constants or wraps functions (e.g. tail_sm40_cap4_size8e9_xsg_off.py: Smirnov-plan size drop, read cap 4, scatter-for-gather off), recorded verbatim in the build record. Python name resolution makes the last definition live, which is why the released file has shadowed definitions.

terms.label: star
terms.meaning: The plane-only remainder of the third-order tensor: the part of K21 represented separately from the signed rank-one column bank. The record contains dense and low-rank star pushes, including a rank-32 detached basis; later files use the direction-based star with _SS_RANK = -1 and per-layer strength _SS_BETA. In the F4 derivation, the fourth-order star means the hub-with-three-smooth-legs diagram.

terms.label: store (VM32 / Mac32) / held-out 25 / fresh / cross-half truth / paired
terms.meaning: The store is a fixed set of 32 ranked networks with cached 2 x 32M-sample Monte Carlo truths used for paired scoring (VM32 on the Linux VM, Mac32 on the Mac); the held-out 25 are the store ranks never used for fitting; fresh = newly generated networks (fresh12, fresh24, seeds 7100000+); cross-half truth = scoring against the two independent truth halves so truth noise cancels (final U); paired = variant and control scored on the same networks (for wall, launched within a minute of each other). Raw effects below ~0.5% cannot be read on 2 or 7 ranks.

terms.label: strength (readout strength x1.5 / x1.35)
terms.meaning: A scalar multiplying the exported readout coefficients (shrinkage): x1.5 on #337619, x1.35 on #337641, the peak of the five-point ladder x1.05/1.2/1.35/1.5/1.65 on the 961-column seal (VM32 adjusted -0.572/-0.654 vs #337506); the optimum moves below 1.5 as columns grow.

terms.label: sync point
terms.meaning: A client-side materialisation of a flopscope array value (tolist(), bool(), float(), int(...)) that forces a server round trip and is charged to the residual; the only ones kept are integer roster counts; #337259 retired 32 of 41 of them.

terms.label: T22 / GTR
terms.meaning: The pair map stores T22_ij = K22_ij / (v_i v_j). In the GTR optimization, the Gaussian series and the T22-weighted derivative series share already-rounded F2*G2 and F3*G3 products. Reusing those products preserves the original reductions and divisions; the T22 plane is not itself a matrix-multiplication kernel.

terms.label: torch card / native / parity
terms.meaning: The torch card is the PyTorch research re-implementation used for training, oracles and screens; it omits several native cost-saving approximations and was 0.7-3.4% more accurate than the native file on 2026-10-01 and 16-19% by 2026-10-20 (decide natively). Native = the flopscope file as scored. Parity = the check that a native port reproduces the torch arm network by network (correlation and size D of the per-unit change).

terms.label: TPS / terminal scale batching
terms.meaning: Batch the terminal output-only scale nodes of Smirnov plans. Intermediate add/subtract nodes retain their operation, order, and destination. The preparation records the output coefficients and applies them as one terminal multiplication.

terms.label: twin (safe twin, clean twin, science twin)
terms.meaning: A second file that differs from a candidate in one setting: the safe twin keeps a safety setting (governor/rescue, depth-7 off) for the designated run; the clean twin has scatter-for-gather off (#337617 = clean twin of #337614); the science twin is the local-evaluation copy of a released file (same estimator under a science-mode wrapper used for paired local scoring). Matt's rule 10-18: no safe-twin fires on the lead's own judgment.

terms.label: u64 law (client call-form measurement)
terms.meaning: The referenced call-form benchmark found roughly 42-45K client instructions per request across call forms and concluded that reducing the request count was the useful residual-time lever. The label identifies the measurement; it does not denote a uint64 numerical law.

terms.label: ubown / UBcluster / cluster
terms.meaning: The ubown route builds a B transform directly in retained independent storage, removing an arena-to-cache copy while charging the new owned bindings. The cluster extension applies related reuse to UBC, UBX, and layer-7 cache routes under their existing caps and owner/prediction lifetimes. These are storage and scheduling changes, not cumulant approximations.

terms.label: UBX / UBC-X / UBX_RC
terms.meaning: UBC-X caches counted copies of the prefix frame's right-operand B transforms for old-tier inner-read products, reusing unchanged transformed values across layers 10-14. UBX_RC adds a prediction-local reconstruction cache for the layer-7 frame and clears it when that frame is no longer used. Owner, generation, shape, and prediction identities delimit reuse.

terms.label: UVP split (u-leg / v-leg)
terms.meaning: In the old-tier frame a birth pair p+- = U (f_u +- f_v/2) is stored as a common part f_u (the u-leg, kept on the frame's leading r_u = 256 coordinates) and a difference part f_v (the v-leg, on all 384 coordinates); the split read and reconstruct in u/v form (_uvp_split, _uvp_recon / _astra_bcc_uvrecon) is the native form, worth -1.3..-1.6% bill.

terms.label: wall (wall clock)
terms.meaning: The per-network wall clock of predict on the hosted grader, capped at 120 s (a TIME_EXHAUSTED network is killed at ~120 s roundtrip and the run is wiped from the board); hosted wall tracks requests (0.71) and puts (0.74), not FLOPs (0.12); the final lineage ran 99-113 s, and #337534 failed on a +10-12% grader slowdown.

terms.label: warm / cold
terms.meaning: Cold = a worker's first prediction (caches, keys and lazy binds not yet made: higher requests and residual); warm = later predictions. The public evaluation is ~95% warm (5 workers x ~20 networks), whereas fresh-process local science bills are cold and overstate compute gains (setup-time/first-use savings are worth ~5% of face value publicly).

terms.label: Winograd / Strassen kernels (packed kernel, cp3, hz, strips)
terms.meaning: Fast matrix-product kernels that perform fewer metered multiplies: recursive Strassen/Winograd-type products over a fixed arena ('audited four/five-level fixed-arena Winograd product', depths 4-7, _CP3_WINOGRAD_LEVELS = 4) with packed push/read view sets (_PACKED_PUSH / _PACKED_READ) bound at setup; the tree leaves are batched matmuls (_hz_leaf and _ipt_leaf_unwind_ab = 67% of the bill), the Winograd adds/subtracts ~8-15%; 'hzs' = half-zero-strip padding kernels (bill -1.2%); kernel rounding is 10-25x BLAS (Frobenius 4-8e-6). Depth trades bill against wall.

terms.label: XSG (scatter-for-gather)
terms.meaning: Gathering rows by a scatter primitive (_xsg_rows / _xsg_cols at nine sites, gated by _XSG_ON) because the meter charged it less than a plain index gather A[idx]; predictions byte-identical, bill 0.077% lower. Judged the one fair-accounting exposure (rules s5.5: a transformation whose only purpose is a cheaper-charged path) and retired (_XSG_ON = set()) in every designated file.

terms.label: YNT (young negative trace)
terms.meaning: The young push at layers 7-14 crops the rows with gate a < -2.5 (dead units) and repairs their contribution by a trace; at layer 14 the pushed young columns feed the final layer's k3 directly (hyper-sensitive), so the crop threshold becomes _YNT_Z = 3.0 for the L13 and L14 pushes only (a per-layer wrapper of _shared_old384_push; the literal 2.5 at the three active sites, including the U/young fusion prepare, reads _YNT_Z). Part of the L14 exactness stack (#337126, #337142): raw -0.23% for +0.11% bill at L14, the L13 rung doubles it, L12 a wash.

terms.label: zb4 (zero-bill dial stack)
terms.meaning: The four zero-bill dial arms with negative store means stacked and appended last by the opus-solo lane: _GK4 1.0, _BFIX_GAMMA 0.119, _GSK 0.9, _SS_BETA 0.85 (store 32 ranks -0.30%, 21/32 lower); these are the dial values the designated files carry (except GK4, later 1.04).

terms.label: ZMS
terms.meaning: The experiment identifies units whose effective learned correction differs from the raw correction and whose resulting mean is exactly zero. It zeros the corresponding covariance rows, columns, and variance entries at layers 1-14. The source calls this a covariance-only hypothesis; it leaves that layer's means and higher-moment targets unchanged.

statuses.open: The question was still unresolved in this record.

statuses.solved: A reusable solution or exact result was established.
statuses.closed_proof: The stated assumptions rule out this approach.
statuses.closed_measured: Measurements ruled out the tested version.
statuses.closed_cost: The approach exceeded the computation budget.

original_status_definitions.open: A concrete unresolved question with a defined next test.
original_status_definitions.testing: A sealed canonical scientific execution is running, or its primary result awaits independent verification and integration.
original_status_definitions.solved: The dependency is understood and a reusable solution or exact result exists.
original_status_definitions.closed_proof: The stated approach is impossible or insufficient under the stated assumptions.
original_status_definitions.closed_measured: A faithful implementation failed its preregistered accuracy test.
original_status_definitions.closed_cost: The approach has capacity but cannot fit the legal compute budget.
original_status_definitions.closed_this_form: This implementation failed; a materially different member of the broader family remains possible.
original_status_definitions.capacity_only: Oracle evidence shows capacity, but no legal recursive provider exists.
original_status_definitions.blocked: A prerequisite experiment has not passed yet.

problem.title: Estimate a network’s mean outputs from its weights
problem.summary: Given the weights of a 16-layer, 1,024-neuron ReLU network and a standard-normal input, estimate every neuron’s mean output.
problem.why_it_is_hard: A mean alone is not enough: the average output of ReLU depends on the shape of its input distribution.
problem.constraint: The submitted estimators propagate statistics without drawing input samples, within strict computation, memory and time limits.
problem.score: The official score combines final-layer mean-squared error with the amount of computation used.

approaches.title: Approximate the distribution analytically
approaches.idea: Start with Gaussian formulas for ReLU means, then add Hermite polynomial terms to capture non-Gaussian effects.
approaches.result: Increasing the polynomial order beyond four gave essentially no improvement; final-layer mean-squared error remained about 3.85 × 10⁻⁶.

next_recorded_edges.reason: Adapt the compressed third-order carrier to 1024x16.

approaches.title: Carry higher moments through the network
approaches.idea: Propagate third- and fourth-order statistics so each layer retains more than means and covariances.
approaches.result: A complete implementation met the resource limits, but its measured error missed the target; some richer stored statistics also failed mathematical consistency checks.

next_recorded_edges.reason: Use learned correction only after the Phase 2 analytic state is fixed.

approaches.title: Learn corrections from training data
approaches.idea: Fit a model to the errors in the propagated statistics and feed its corrections into later layers.
approaches.result: Accurate reference inputs showed enough correction capacity, but the tested models could not reproduce that accuracy using only quantities available during inference.
approaches.next_label: Examine the information missing in later layers

approaches.title: Recover information lost in later layers
approaches.idea: Identify which carried statistics cause the remaining error, then try to calculate better ones from the weights.
approaches.result: The tested signed-pair correction failed; separate diagnostics located late-layer error in the propagated state and left direct construction of better corrections open.
approaches.next_label: Compare the cost of the alternatives

approaches.title: Reduce computation without losing accuracy
approaches.idea: Improve the official score by reducing arithmetic while preserving the prediction.
approaches.result: Discarding more information hurt accuracy; changes to the implementation produced real cost savings, although one replacement still failed only in official submission.

approaches.title: Verify the complete estimators
approaches.idea: Check accuracy across networks, repair rare failures, and evaluate the complete source under the official limits.
approaches.result: All 11 unusually large-error cases in a 688-network scan were repaired; a later learned correction reached about 2.94 × 10⁻⁸ raw mean-squared error in official evaluation.
approaches.next_label: See what the released estimators contain

reading.reading_order_semantics: Navigation among approach groups only. Only the explicit recorded_connections list may be drawn as scientific/decomposition edges.
